Last year, we broke our teeth. A powerful return from the East had begun on the first scheduled day of the raid and ended… on the last. This year, the conditions are almost the opposite: heavy snow up to low altitude, windless anticyclone, clear light. Only problem, an avalanche risk still announced at 4 at the start.
Je décide donc d'inverser le sens de la: I therefore decide to reverse the direction of the crossing: Limone Piemonte towards Garessio 2000. Five days between the Po plain and the Mediterranean, four unguarded huts, hundreds of chamois and almost total solitude. Not a skier, not a trace. In the Alps, this is rare.

Cela faisait des mois que l'on en discut: We had been talking about it for months. The idea excited me. It stirred something in me and was to be the high point of a winter season devoted almost entirely to ski journeys. To begin a traverse of the Alps in segments, over 20 years, with a group of clients I had known for three years. To begin it in the best possible way, crossing a little-known range at the first or last end of the Alps: the Ligurian Alps, from Garessio to Limone.
Everything started for the best though. Finding ourselves in a small restaurant in Garessio, impatient at the idea of ​​starting an adventure, we didn't think that Gianluca was as motivated as us to party and live in the moment. It all ended at 4 a.m., with a final bottle of Barolo. This is what we came to look for. Actually nothing special, but everything that could happen, especially if it wasn't planned.
L'issue du lendemain l'était d'ailleurs: The outcome the next day was even more so. We knew it. All the models had anticipated this return from the East. And day by day, its intensity grew. But we had to go up to Garessio 2000 station to see it physically. The goal became obvious. Gianluca told us about another hut on the southern slope. Let’s go see…
Le vent nous a fait vaciller mais il a l: The wind made us waver but it left our determination intact. Unshakeable, even when discovering the small room serving as a winter hut: a 5 m² space with three bunk beds. There were 6 of us! I persisted in this plan, but now I had to face the facts: the Ligurian Alps would be inhospitable this year, in the allotted window. After a night “recessed”, feeling the vibrations of the structure caused by the gusts, we had to make the decision.
Le moral des troupes n'était pas haut, a: The morale of the troops was not high, in the middle of Fossano station, when we were eating a picnic that we would have preferred to share up there. After many plans, the Aosta Valley still seemed the best option. We are all jubilant at the thought of not going home so soon. Perhaps a little less Guillaume and Mat, whose mission was to find the car parked in Limone and remove its thick white siding – at least 60 cm!
Le Val d'Aoste, c'est un peu ma deuxième: The Aosta Valley is a bit like my second home. I had two plans, pretty certain ones. After a phone call to a guide friend from Aosta Valley, we opted for the plan located closest to the border, a guarantee this year of better snow cover.
Une itinérance magnifique, entre le bivo: A magnificent journeying, between the still secret Cosimo Zappelli bivouac and the Deffeyes hut, at the foot of the imposing Ruitor glaciers. Nobody and not a trace of skiing for three days, yet just a stone's throw from Courmayeur. All this will always surprise me! And a final memorable descent, in a unique canyon with a 1000 m drop, punctuated by a small jump not so expected on the map!
L’an passé, on s’était cassé les dents,: Last year, we broke our teeth, arriving in the Ligurian Alps on the first day of a powerful return from the East, starting on the first planned day of the raid and ending on the last day... Cette année, les conditions sont bien di: This year, the conditions are very different. For two weekends, the returns from the East have generously adorned the southern Alps with a white blanket down to low altitude, and they are forecasting a windless anticyclone. This is the perfect opportunity to try the adventure again, in more serene conditions.
Seul hic : le risque d’avalanches est en: Only problem: the risk of avalanches is still announced at 4 on the day of our departure. In Italy, I have the sword of Damocles above my head. Particularly for this reason, I decided to reverse the direction of the crossing: this time we will leave from Limone Piemonte to finish at Garessio 2000, on the edge of the Alps!
Tout a été incroyable : la vue dégagée s: Everything was incredible: the unobstructed view over the entire Alpine arc thanks to the contrasts of colours between the green Po plain and the snow-capped mountains, the view of the Mediterranean Sea on the other side, the soft lights perfect for photos, the 4 unguarded cabins in which we slept... And above all: the solitude. Although we encountered hundreds of chamois, we did not encounter a skier or a trace during these five days of crossing. In the Alps, this is rare!
Les emplois du temps se sont parfaitemen: The schedules lined up perfectly, and two days after my arrival at Garessio 2000 after a fantastic ride in the Ligurian Alps and after a marathon day to finalize and (finally) send the final version of my thesis manuscript, I had the chance to leave from the same station of Limone Piemonte, but this time heading north and initiating a crossing of the Alps in segments, the common thread for the next 20 years.

Après notre fantastique chevauchée dans: After our fantastic ride in the Ligurian Alps, to the borders of the Alps, I found myself alone in Vinadio, with the heavy burden of submitting my thesis manuscript.  After 7 years where “Thérèse” was a daily obsession, Vinadio and its Caffè della Piazza were my last port, the ultimate ephemeral office.
Le soir, une bonne équipe me rejoint, av: In the evening, a good team joined me, with the plan of initiating a crossing of the Alps over several years. For the first stage, we planned a half crossing of the Argentera massif. Long stages await us, both in terms of elevation and distance. And there were some twists and turns!
Le premier soir, après une belle étape d: The first evening, after a nice stopover in the pine and larch forests, we arrive at night in a cabin that I would not have trouble classifying as one of the most rustic visited this winter. The concrete walls, already damp before our visit, were not fixed by this one. The beds are bunk, three stories high, equipped with box springs. Blankets are rationed: one soft and comfortable and one rustic per person. Fortunately, we arrived there late and we planned to leave at dawn. The night is cool.

Le deuxième jour, Sylvain doit nous quit: The second day, Sylvain had to leave us suddenly, following a bad fall the day before which did not leave his thigh unscathed. For the third time in my career, I was forced to call transalpine emergency services. The helicopter will be slow to arrive, and we are not early to finish our stage. A beautiful west slope awaits us, steep as can be, with a small dry skiing section to get out. This slope was a grey area in my preparation, and we are doing well, without needing to go down too low. Another slope worries me: we have to climb quite high towards the Pagari hut to reach by gravity a small exposed passage, which I would like to be able to cross on the descent. It goes without problem! We still have one last climb to reach our second cabin. Except that once we get to the point where we should see it, there is nothing. Only a steep snow slope.
Je me remémore alors cette expérience du: I then remember this experience of the small Blais bivouac, located just under the crest of the French-Italian border, where during the night the wind had brought nearly a metre of snow in front of the door, forcing us to redouble our ingenuity to open the door from the inside. The configuration of this bivouac is identical, located under a ridge. I had the good idea to record aerial maps of the area where the bivouac is clearly visible. It only took a few probes to identify the location of the door. And after an hour of shoveling, the entrance to the bivouac is clear! What is certain is that we were not cold that night.

Le lendemain, c’est Roland qui ne se sen: The next day, it's Roland who doesn't feel well, still on antibiotics after a bad bout of bronchitis. I have to organise his repatriation, this time without a helicopter because he was not prevented from skiing on the descent. What followed was an endless day, weighed down by the heat. There was again the episode of the reservoir lake, which we had to cross. Missing the small tunnel of the summer path, partly blocked by snow, we found ourselves doing urban ski-mountaineering along an imposing concrete structure... then there was finally this path to go down to arrive at the Valdieri thermal baths. No less was needed for skiing.
Valdieri, Casa Savoia, enfin, on va mang: Valdieri, Casa Savoia, finally, we will eat something other than Rana, finally we can quench our thirst with a great beer and enjoy good Piedmontese wines. While the evening was as sluggish as our fatigue, it was suddenly revived when four Italian women entered the hut, in a completely improbable way, taken from the depths of the dark night.

Refuge Valasco, on profite d’une petite: Valasco Refuge, we enjoy a little drink break, in the heart of the spring heatwave. Strange hut, straight out of a fairy tale or a leftover from the set of a fantasy film. I'm taking advantage of the wifi to schedule yet another change in weather plans for the upcoming weekend. It’s not an easy task to find shelter for 12 on a Saturday evening in March. On the climb that follows, we finally come across skiers. It’s Claude, a Swiss guide who I advised a few days ago to come to the area.
Refuge Malinvern, perché là-haut sur son: Malinvern Refuge, perched up there on its promontory. The winter room, also high up, enjoys a magnificent view of the valley.
La dernière étape remplit toutes ses pro: The last stage fulfills all its promises: the landscape is open and once again sparse with small larch trees. We decide to go up to the Cima Gias dei Laghi, in particular to see the rest of our crossing. Next year we will try to sleep at the imposing Sant’Anna hospice. It's hard to leave because the view is so captivating. Another good descent sheltered from the sun, before finding Sylvain where the snow no longer covers the road.
Cette demi-traversée de l’Argentera a re: This half-crossing of the Argentera fulfilled all its promises. Beautiful, long stages, very varied landscapes, rustic and sometimes playful huts, descents that remained cold and sometimes became very soft. Meetings too, with the guards of Valdieri, with grouse roosters and dozens of chamois.

La météo étant perturbée dans les Tödi p: The weather being disturbed in the Tödi then in the Silvretta, I fell back on the Argentera, a massif already crossed in 2015 then found again in 2024 and 2025 during my crossing of the Alps.
Sept jours d'Entracque à Sant'Anna di Va: Seven days from Entracque to Sant’Anna di Valdieri, via Casterino and the huts of Nice, Cougourde, Remondino, Valasco and Livio Bianco. A range well suited to a ski journey, with abundant snow this year and room to put together gentle or committing days. Above all, around the bend on one stage, my first encounter with wolves, in broad daylight, just a few dozen metres away.

D'Entracque à Sant'Anna di Valdieri, une: From Entracque to Sant'Anna di Valdieri, a transalpine crossing via Casterino and a succession of huts open in winter.
Depuis Entracque, montée par le vallon d: From Entracque, climb through the Ischietto valley - wild terrain, large avalanche deposits crossed along the way - then first switch on the French side to Casterino.
Depuis Casterino, presque en ligne droit: From Casterino, almost in a straight line via the Baisse de Fontanalbe then the Baisse du Basto, in the wind and the snow carried. The route also passes by the summit of Mont Clapier (3045 m), calm despite the wind, before reaching the Nice hut.

Depuis Remondino, montée à la Cima di Le: From Remondino, climb to the Cima di Leccia via the Cerise pass, then cross the Baisse de Rogué and the Tête des Bresses Sud, before descending to the Valasco hut, the former hunting pillbox of Victor-Emmanuel II.

Une traversée transalpine sous le signe: A transalpine crossing under the sign of wind, wolves and improvisation
Ce matin, il règne une ambiance à la foi: This morning, there is an atmosphere that is both light and serious. Light because it will probably be necessary to improvise, and this dose of uncertainty which does not allow us to plan ahead opens up the field of our possibilities. It opens the day with intoxicating unknowns.
Grave, parce que nous sommes silencieuse: Serious, because we are silently aware of the conditions that await us once we pass through the door. No promises today. We are the first to leave the shelter. Outside, it is snowing and the wind is gusty. Every inch of my face is covered. Only the eyes, through my glasses, can see.
Je pense à ces femmes qui ne peuvent res: I think of these women who cannot breathe freely through their noses. To Afghan women and all others. I think of the Taliban, who so quickly took over the reins of a country that was nevertheless on a path to freedom.
« Il y a quelqu'un au col ! », je m'écri: “There’s someone at the pass!” », I exclaim. A slender silhouette, a bag on its back, stands in the indentation, projecting its being into the whiteness of the sky. Where could it come from? The other side is even wilder than the one we are going up. And no, the illusion doesn't last long. It's a sign. I am both disappointed and happy. Happy to know we are alone in this mountain which doubts the validity of our presence.
De l'autre côté du col, le refuge Figari: On the other side of the pass, the Figari hut, closed at this time, and the Chiotas reservoir give the feeling of a reassuring presence. However, they are inanimate concrete beings. Inert things. But they serve as landmarks, and probably also as shelter in the event of an unforeseen event.
Le tour du Kaçkar, en Turquie, s'est tra: The tour of Kaçkar, in Türkiye, turned into a Rätikon-Silvretta crossing, in Switzerland and Austria. Because of Trump and his senseless war in the Middle East. And the Swiss trip has become transalpine for a legitimate cause of the mountaineer, almost a refrain in this particularly snowy winter of 2026: the weather.
Une, deux, puis trois réponses négatives: One, two, then three negative answers for the shelters. Back to the start. And why not do the crossing in the other direction? Very often, it is in these kinds of constraints that the greatest opportunities appear.
Ce sera donc une traversée d'Entracque à: It will therefore be a crossing from Entracque to Sant'Anna di Valdieri, passing through Casterino and the huts of Nice, Cougourde, Remondino, Valasco and Livio Bianco. And if possible deviating from obvious lines. With the barely hidden objective of seeing the wolves of Argentera again.
Entre les refuges Livio Bianco et Valasc: Between the Livio Bianco and Valasco shelters, a few days before, with Alexis, Géraud and Laurent, I finally saw the wolf. A trio, surprised to see skiers sliding down, and in turn sliding down the slope. Furtive encounter, pleasure consumed but surely not shared with these individuals who usually do not make themselves seen.
Des traces, nous en croiserons dès le pr: We will come across traces from the first day, at the entrance to the Ischietto valley, leaving the Sabbione valley on the left. A vast steep and hilly slope faces us. At the intersection of these two options, no one wanted to decide between the peaceful option of Sabbione and the more adventurous option of Ischietto. So, in the absence of votes for the easy option, I decided for the unknown.
Un trou dans la neige, maculé de sang su: A hole in the snow, stained with blood on its edges. At the bottom, a butchered chamois, whose legs are still very fleshy, with pink meat. Obviously, the feast was eaten, and the remains were placed in a cool place. A little further on, we cross a huge avalanche deposit. As I climb up one of its side slopes, I am suddenly surprised by an unexpected flight. A golden eagle has just deployed its full wingspan just below me, while it was busy tearing the neck of a dead young chamois. So many encounters!
Avec Gilles, nous nous partageons la tra: With Gilles, we share the trail. Soon I see it disappear in the swirls of snow carried by the wind. An unpleasant preview of the conditions we will have to face over the next few days.
Casterino est un village saisonnier. Une: Casterino is a seasonal village. Around ten buildings, and almost half tourist accommodation. Against all expectations, snow covers all the surrounding slopes. A decade since Paul has seen this much snow, this late in the season. Resolutely the year of Mediterranean skiing, in all its latitudes.
La mer sera notre toile de fond pour les: The sea will be our backdrop for the days to come, a deep, infinite blue horizon, contrasting with the snowy slopes and pine forests.
Deux skieurs de randonnée dans un vallon: Two cross-country skiers in a snowy valley in Mercantour
Montée à ski dans une vallée enneigée du: Ski climb in a snowy valley of Mercantour
On sent les Préalpes, les montagnes s'ap: We feel the Pre-Alps, the mountains resemble hills, soft shapes covered with larch trees. The wind picks us up as we leave the forest, never to let go. There is no longer any question of making detours to reach the Nice hut: Baisse de Fontanalbe and Baisse de Basto constitute almost a perfect azimuth.
On pense être protégés en se mettant sou: We think we are protected by placing ourselves under the prevailing wind. A sort of canyon, bordered to the north by a cliff, could be saving. But the wind is so strong that it turns alternately in all directions, without giving us the slightest respite. We are like the characters in La Horde du Contrevent, forced to develop collective strategies in the face of this element which little by little imposes itself as the heart of the experience.
Au mont Clapier, il n'y a presque plus u: At Mont Clapier, there is almost no breath of air, and the horizon extends to the sea.
Toute la nuit, le vent a tenté de faire: All night long, the wind tried to make the shelter vibrate with gusts. But even the strongest among them did nothing to this stone construction with its thick walls. I like to feel the elements unleashed, thus protected. They are close, perceptible, but they do not reach us.
Christophe attaque sa vingt-sixième anné: Christophe is entering his twenty-sixth year of guarding the Nice shelter. A quiet strength, with his coarse mesh cap screwed on his head. Here, as in La Cougourde, you have to be determined and love your job to welcome winter. Half a thousand nights, without running water and without the possibility of helicopter transport to transport food, due to the national park.

Nous repartons au milieu des bourrasques: We set off again amid the squalls, towards the shoulder of Mount Gelas. Certain gusts instantly stop the slightest movement and the “downwind” nature of the place has little effect. But once again, by an incomprehensible physical mechanism or the action of I don't know what divinity, the wind stops at the summit.
Après quelques heures lors desquelles ch: After a few hours during which everyone retreats into their different protective layers, where everyone follows the rhythm imposed by the wind, we reach the Cougourde hut. By switching behind the Pas des Ladres, the vegetation appears denser than before. A southern forest that mixes pines and larches, an ideal terrain for wolves.
Alors que je repars, toujours dans la mê: As I leave again, still in the same quest to tire Gilles, towards Cima Gaisse, they will see them, the wolves. Right opposite, from the small windows of the shelter. A trio, like the previous week.
Quant à nous, je chercherai non sans dét: As for us, I will not hesitate to look for the key to the entrance to the northwest couloir. After trying to get back halfway up the slope, finding myself above a small continuous rocky bar, then trying to follow the dotted blue line indicated on the map, finding myself again above high bars, we resigned ourselves to putting the skins back on to attempt access from the summit.
L'accès au couloir est d'ici plus éviden: Access to the couloir is more obvious from here, although some doubt remains since a large rock seems to block access to the lower part. It just passes, and the rest is delicious to ski. On our way back, some news, and what news! Three wolves passed by, in broad daylight, right in front of the shelter.
Quentin, presque trentenaire, est gardie: Quentin, almost thirty years old, has been a winter caretaker since this year at Cougourde. Only the small stove warms the room. Here too, opening in winter requires loving your job.

Aujourd'hui, nous basculons en Italie, p: Today, we move to Italy, for the second half of the raid which I decidedly thought was transalpine, since three huts are guarded: Remondino, Valasco and Livio Bianco.
Un beau couloir ne m'était pas apparu in: A beautiful couloir did not initially appear obvious to me, and its presence allows you to switch to Lake Chiotas with a certain logic, auguring a beautiful descent from the Cima dell'Agnel. The wind has subsided, but it welcomes us at the summit in an icy manner, before falling completely silent in the valley of Lake Chiotas.
Pour une fois, nous rejoignons le refuge: For once, we reach the shelter early. Remondino was not on the initial line: one option among others in the kaleidoscope of possibilities.

Après un petit couloir remonté en crampo: After a small couloir climbed up with crampons, cold windy snow, hard and compact underfoot, we actually arrive at the Cima di Leccia. The sea, from here, becomes the main horizon of our gaze. On the opposite slope, the snow has taken the Mediterranean sun, its surface is hard, almost icy. And the steep slope.
J'esquisse deux virages sautés, courts,: I make two short, jumping turns only to realise that it is not reasonable to have my clients ski down here, even in a skid. The grip is not good enough, there is no room for error. There is no more rational calculation, only an intuition which tells me that it would not be reasonable.
Nous rejoignons un versant aux pentes do: We reach a slope with gentle slopes, covered with pine and larch forests. A land of wolves. And indeed, the clues do not have to wait long. Several parallel traces, characterized by large pads, descend the slope of the Basse de Rogue.
Un dernier coup d'œil à la mer depuis la: One last look at the sea from the head of Bresses Sud, and we dive into the opposite slope. The wind blew too much, making the coat sometimes hard, sometimes uncertain for support.
Valasco, un refuge étrange. Ancienne cas: Valasco, a strange hut. Former hunting casemate of Victor-Emmanuel II, two towers mark the entrance to a large interior courtyard, like a riad. Tables and deckchairs are an invitation to beer. There is a special atmosphere there: the conviviality of reunions after a good day of skiing.
Après une assiette variée d'antipasti, u: After a varied plate of antipasti, a table is set up just behind the bar. Large bowls and half a wheel of gorgonzola take place there: one is filled with polenta, the other with the traditional salsiccia in umido dish, including sausages in tomato sauce. As in the self-service restaurant, everyone comes to help themselves as they wish after Andrea has garnished each plate with a generous ladle of polenta. This little nothing livens up the room and gives a joyful atmosphere.

Depuis plusieurs hivers, le massif de la: For several winters, the Bernina massif had made me want to explore on skis. For this last major raid of the 2026 season, a four-day weather window finally allowed us to leave: Diavolezza, Fortezza, Boval, the hanging glaciers, the moraines and the high altitude bivouacs.
Deux alpinistes progressent à skis au pi: Two mountaineers progress on skis at the foot of the seracs.

Reconstruit à partir de la trace GPS rée: Reconstructed from the actual GPS track of the raid: Diavolezza, Fortezza, Boval hut, Tschierva glacier, Pizzo Bernina and Piz Palü.
Depuis la station supérieure de Diavolez: From the Diavolezza upper station, descent to the Vadret Pers, then crossing the glacier towards the foot of the Fortezza. Ascend Vadret da Fortezza and cross the Fortezza ridge, before a long descent towards the Vadret da Morteratsch basin. Crossing the glacier then going up the moraine to Chamanna da Boval, at 2,495 m.
Chamanna da Boval → Bivacco Agostino Par: Chamanna da Boval → Bivacco Agostino Parravicini
De Boval, remontée vers le Vadret Boval: From Boval, go up towards Vadret Boval then cross the Fuorcla Misaun. The trace continues towards Fuorcla da Boval, around 3,346 m, then switches to Vadrettin da Tschierva to reach Chamanna da Tschierva exactly. After descending into the Tschierva/Roseg glacial system, a long traverse south and back up to Fuorcla da la Sella, at 3,253 m. From there, pass on the Italian side to the Bivacco Agostino Parravicini, perched at 3,183 m above the Vedretta di Scerscen Superiore.
Bivacco Parravicini → Bivacco Pansera, v: Bivacco Parravicini → Bivacco Pansera, via Piz Bernina
Depuis Parravicini, traversée de la Vedr: From Parravicini, crossing the Vedretta di Scerscen Superiore towards the Passo Marinelli Occidentale. The route continues eastwards to the Bivacco Pansera sector, reached for the first time during the day, then begins a large altitude loop: ascent towards the Pass dal Zupò, crossing the Cresta Guzza sector, then the normal Bernina route via La Spedla - the Italian shoulder at around 4,020 m - before precisely reaching Piz Bernina, the highest point of the raid at 4,048 m. After the summit, return east on the high massif, then traverse to Fuorcla Bellavista and return to Bivacco Pansera, where the trail stops for the night at around 3,540 m.
Départ avant l'aube depuis le Bivacco Pa: Departure before dawn from Bivacco Pansera. Going up towards the western ridge of the Palü massif, passing through the Piz Spinas sector, then crossing Piz Palü: the route precisely reaches its central summit around 3,900 m, then continues towards its eastern summit. Long descent then on the northern slope, via the Vadret Pers glacial system, before reaching Bernina Diavolezza, in the valley, at around 2,090 m - the bottom station, and not the upper station of Diavolezza (2,978 m).
Cela fait au moins trois hivers que ce p: This small massif to the east of the Alps has been making me want to explore on skis for at least three winters, and each year I have multiplied the possible routes on my map application, sometimes starting from St. Moritz or Diavolezza in Switzerland, sometimes from Campo Moro, in Italy.
Et puis vient ce dernier grand raid de l: And then comes this last big raid of the 2026 season, where I have to share an experience with two twin brothers, who are celebrating their four decades, straddling the months of April and May. I'm throwing this idea out there. The remote nature of the place does not seem to frighten them and the weather window becomes clearer: a small disturbance passes on Wednesday, but from Thursday to Sunday, the weather becomes stable, before changing again the following Monday. A bargain!
Lorsque nous nous garons sur le grand pa: When we park in the large car park at the foot of the Diavolezza cable car, it is huge and almost empty. The atmosphere is spring-like, only a little fresh air reminds us that we have come to ski. There is also the ski slope, already descended by some die-hard skiers. Diavolezza, strange name. Why is the devil, present in a suggestive way in the station's communication, summoned to name a tourist place? What the hell is he doing here! Unanswered question, but undisguised pleasure at reaching the foot of the glaciers so quickly. Perhaps the image of the devil translates both the splendor and the dangerousness of these immense serac bars which strike the eye of anyone arriving at the top of the cable car, when the panorama opens up extending from Piz Palü to Bernina, and its innumerable suspended and chaotic glaciers. Few Alpine massifs reflect these images. And paradoxically, this impressive character is counterbalanced by the relatively modest size of the massif, which can be toured in three or four days.
Nous ressentons le printemps, et peut-êt: We feel spring, and maybe even summer, when we set foot on the glacier. There is not a breath of air. On this glacier, there are millions of small creatures, elongated in shape and measuring only a few millimeters. This is the first time I have encountered this phenomenon, but not without being surprised by their number, and the abilities that these insects develop to be able to live here, in the snow.
Nous traversons le glacier en direction: We cross the glacier towards a tongue of snow, a sort of scarf between the rocky bars. While we endured the heat, I almost unconsciously chose a ventilated place for a picnic: the ridge coming from “Fortezza”, our objective for the day. It forms a comfortable shoulder to go up on skis, protected on either side by rocky bars, which soon also take over the ridge to form this famous “fortress”. From there, a new scarf takes us to the opposite glacier, and to the Boval cabin, built well above the moraine, immense here. Moreover, access to the hut seems to cross this moraine in its zone of weakness, which seems a little less steep and relatively stabilized. After some careful consideration about the possibility of putting the skins back on for a short climb, given the quality of the uneven snow, we opted without much hesitation for a beer on the terrace. My companions seem relatively worried at the prospect of lacking some in the coming days, when we will be in an unguarded cabin, and they seem to want to compensate in advance for this lack. I can't imagine putting my carbon Gignoux in all these protruding and unstable rocks, so I leave the shells and keep only the liners. And it's ultimately much more comfortable.
Le pari s'avère gagnant : une terrasse a: The bet turns out to be a winner: a terrace in the sun, and the solitude of a hut where we will be almost alone this evening. The guard, Roberto, seems boorish at first. Not very chatty, but he still makes the effort to speak a mix of French and English, to bring us three large draft beers. He has been guarding this hut for twenty-two years after four years at the Forno cabin, and I feel he is tired of being there. One or two years and it will be retirement for this ski instructor from Pontresina who never really seems to stop working. He is also waiting for two people from Eastern countries who have booked, but who do not seem to honor their commitment, an attitude which seems to make our host resigned, who describes them as "stupid people". A behaviour which has continued to gain importance in recent years, perhaps helped by the ease and dehumanization of exchanges allowing reservations to be made in shelters. So there are only three of us in the refectory, with fine service and a “Swiss-style” menu, the soup always being followed by green salad, and the dessert, based on meringue.
Un skieur remonte le glacier en directio: A skier goes up the glacier towards the Bernina peaks.

Quand nous descendons au réfectoire, à 6: When we go down to the refectory at 6 a.m., the two other skiers who arrived late the day before have already left. Unconsciously, this day stresses me out. I don't know if it's because of its length, combined with the fact that I don't really know my companions, or the unknownness of the passages and the opposite slope, where in 2024 a gigantic collapse swept away the Vadret de Tschierva. There is just enough snow to reach the valley from Piz Misaun. The Forcia Misaun passage is a scarf of snow, partly exposed and, from below, not very welcoming. Yannaël and Erwan are uncomfortable with this passage, and I immediately feel them questioning my strategy and my route choices. I prefer to raise the scarf from the bottom, and not try to take the snow slope which seems to offer a shortcut. From the breach, a scree, then a path cleared of snow and equipped with cables crosses in the middle of a rocky bar. Finally a good-natured ice cream parlor!
De la Fuorcia Tschierva, la neige manque: From the Fuorcia Tschierva, there is still no snow, and the slope into which we fall, on the imposing Vadret Tschierva, is immense and mineral. As spotted the previous evening on satellite images, we will have to cross the moraine on foot. The snow is already rare in the first part of the descent, but we are doing well. Until the slope becomes really steeper, making it easier for the snow to melt. And making our progress more complex. Unstable slopes, certainly steep, but so easy to descend with skis on, quickly become an ordeal in ski boots. We join a path, and descend towards an unknown which seems more and more uncertain to me, as the ground beneath our feet becomes clearer. After crossing a rocky bar using a chain, I go scouting. We can clearly see a ski mark on the glacier, just in front of us, and I wonder where these skiers could have set foot there. After crossing along a vague path, I find myself facing an impassable moraine narrows. I'm starting to be very perplexed about the rest of the journey, because what opens up to my gaze is particularly chaotic. I change my mode of action. Now we will design the rest of the programme problem by problem, trying to put all possible options on the table. Go to the Tschierva hut, have a picnic and then report back. At the shelter, I try to open each door, with the vain hope that the winter room is open, contrary to what is indicated on its website. All are closed, well locked, without any play. This option does not work. I am angry with these guards who, here as in Coaz, no longer open their winter rooms. These emergency points, safety zones or simply these wild stops that crisscross the mountain are places for composing improvised experiences for the guide that I am, but this absence for a turn of the key is frustrating.
Je pars devant avec une certaine hâte, p: I go ahead with a certain haste, to scout. Give me time to refine the options before Yannaël and Erwan arrive. We follow the descent path, towards the moraine. It branches off just before, but a path leads towards it, giving the feeling of a possible crossing point. The moraine is steep, but passable. It is thus possible to reach an intermittent snow slope opposite, and from there, the upper part of the flat area of ​​the Tschierva glacier. Except that a rocky bar prevents us from accessing it. Only a tiny, less stiff scarf seems to cross it. If that doesn't work, then we will have to go around via the snow-cleared moraine. A little ordeal. After turning a little to find the entrance to the scarf, I am jubilant to see that my passage works, and to know that the end of this “moraine tunnel” is close. For me but especially for my companions, who release juice in these passages.

Si bien qu'il n'est pas très tôt quand n: So much so that it is not very early when we attack the first picnic, and even later when we attack the climb in sneakers, skis on our backs. We come across an elder in a Duster who insists on showing us the start of the path, although we tried to tell him that we had the map. But he seemed so excited to see a group of young skiers…
Après 500 m à pied, nous chaussons enfin: After 500 m on foot, we finally put on our skis to go up through soft snow along the Rindertal, then, in the sunset lights, to the Furtwangsattel. With a nice scraping session, we reach the slopes overlooking the Windegghütte, regularly crusty then becoming more and more supportive as we go down.
Une petite cabane d'hiver, très conforta: A small winter cabin, very comfortable, with a wood stove and wood that we will be slow to find!

La CSV de la veille nous a alertés sur l: The CSV from the day before alerted us to the steep and potentially hard and exposed slopes which allow us to leave the cabin at the bottom. We reach the impressive Tibetan Triftbrücke bridge, attraction at the start of the day.
La longue combe que nous remontons ensui: The long valley that we then climb up inspires us to take a coffee break, lying in the grass, lulled by the sound of the stream. The break already at the pass to the west of the Giglistock will cost us visibility during the descent of the Gigligletscher…
La neige s'alourdit à mesure que nous pe: The snow gets heavier as we lose altitude, so much so that we prefer to scrape along the crossing at the end rather than risk turns. We then go up the canyon to Steingletscher, where Thomas welcomes us very warmly.
Aprem belote, chill et échange avec Dani: Afterwards belote, chill and chat with Daniel Dulac who I hadn't met for a long time. It's good, the comfort of a good hot shower, sometimes, in the middle of a trip to ski touring. And also to be served food and to open the tap to get water!

La journée crasseuse de la semaine. Elle: The filthy day of the week. It was announced from the start, and the models were not mistaken...
Nous partons sous une épaisse couche de: We leave under a thick layer of fog, in which we soon find ourselves. The snow is softened. At the Obertaljoch pass, we discuss which option we take on the descent: steep and due north, or less steep and west. Some doubt the slope and, without hesitation, we switch to the left.
La neige tombée les jours précédents est: The snow that fell the previous days is placed on a hard bottom, and the whole is homogeneous and quite pleasant to ski. Except for the poor visibility. I opt for an intermediate option, and we soon dive to the right, to find the cold side. We find ourselves on a steep slope, in which we have no choice but to repaint.
La remontée du Wendengletscher se déroul: The ascent of the Wendengletscher takes place in thick fog, conditions which make the small Grassen bivouac, perched high on the ridge dominated by the imposing wall of the Titlis, all the more welcoming.
Nous passerons l'après-midi et la soirée: We will spend the afternoon and evening warmed by the wood fire, listening to the wind and snow whipping the walls of the bivouac.

Lever 6 h, en espérant apprécier le leve: Up at 6 a.m., hoping to enjoy the sunrise. We are disillusioned by seeing the different layers of clouds and fog at all altitudes. I decide to procrastinate.
Mais une heure plus tard, tout semble ch: But an hour later, everything seems to change very quickly, and we rush to leave as soon as possible. Indeed, the layers are successively torn, giving way, finally, to the sun. As the price of this brutal change, the wind picks us up as we leave the bivouac.
Nous décidons de monter au Grassen, somm: We decide to climb Grassen, a summit located at 2946 m, to enjoy the view of the imposing Titlis wall, and from up there, a magical landscape opens up, the summits being revealed by the sea of clouds which extends as far as the eye can see.
Nous traversons à flanc, jusqu'à rejoind: We cross on the side, until reaching a beautiful powder slope. We are reaping the rewards of the disruption of the last few days. Out of overzealousness, I find myself a little low compared to the ski track, which seems to pass through the middle of the cliff. I'm surprised at this failure.
Nous remontons une pente raide et étroit: We go up a steep and narrow slope, which gives us access again to the glaciers of this incredible suspended crossing, to reach the summit of Bärenhorn.
En dessous, la mer de nuages, toujours,: Below, the sea of clouds, still, under which we soon ski. Like the day before, visibility is reduced to zero, and I orient myself using GPS. The snow is getting heavier, and we have to stay at the bottom of the couloir to hope to avoid the tricky stones.
Il nous faut encore traverser une morain: We still have to cross an almost completely snow-free moraine and make a long scraping crossing to finally reach the hut.
La surprise est plutôt bonne : s'il est: The surprise is rather good: if it is less cozy than the previous ones, it is on the other hand new and comfortable, and well stocked with beer. Perhaps just missing a wood stove which would have softened the rather cool atmosphere.
Grande aiguille dominant le glacier pend: Large needle towering over the glacier during the Dammastock–Titlis crossing in the Swiss Alps, on day 4 of journeying.
Réveil matinal, le premier de cette sais: Wake up early, the first of this winter season. It smells like spring! At 5:30 a.m., we are on skis for a seamless warm-up, on an icy slope where we must not fall. Skidding for everyone!
Je ne comprends pas la trace de ski de r: I don't understand the track of ski touring indicated on the Swiss maps, which seems to be easy-going, but the terrain is quite different: steep, icy.
Nous rejoignons le fond de vallon et rem: We reach the bottom of the valley and go up opposite, in the middle of a micro-ski resort. Quickly, we find very wild terrain and, as we rise, we have a breathtaking view of the Titlis and the crossing on the ridges of the day before.

La Haute-Svanétie est un territoire fron: Upper Svaneti is a border territory in the full sense of the word. Geographical border, materialized by the great glacial wall of the Caucasus, but also political and historical. Here, the peaks — Chkhara, Tetnuldi, Ushba — embody a limit. It is in this in-between that this high ski route takes place, from Oushgouli to Iskari.
Je connais cette région depuis une décen: I have known this region for a decade and this is the first time I have come there on skis. Fresh snow, immense glaciers, serac falls: the mountain quickly imposes its rules. But this journey is also played out in the evening, in cabins and villages, around overcrowded tables, chacha and Svan hospitality. With Shako Margiani, IFMGA guide and native of the country, we don't just cross a massif: we enter a little into its history.

Géorgie : Haute Route de la Haute-Svanét: Georgia: Upper Svaneti High Route at ski touring
La Mingrélie-Haute-Svanétie est une des: Mingrelia-Upper Svaneti is one of the twelve regions of Georgia. It extends from the Black Sea to the high peaks of the Caucasus, which marks the Russian-Georgian border. Several high peaks make up this natural border: Chkhara (5193m) and its nine peaks, the highest point in Georgia and third highest peak in the Caucasus; the Djangha (5059m); the Tetnuldi peak (4858m), which could be compared to Mont Blanc and finally Mount Ouchba and its two imposing peaks (4710m). The Upper Svaneti Haute Route is a ski traverse which crosses from Ouchgouli, at the foot of Chkhara, to Iskari, southwest of Ouchba. This route was carried out by guides Yann Borgnet and Shako Margiani and their 9 clients from 4–10 April 2024. Story.
Je suis déjà allé deux fois en Géorgie,: I have already been to Georgia twice, in Upper Svaneti. The first time, in 2014, when the country was just emerging from a still perceptible escalation of tensions with its Russian neighbour, already engaged in imperial desires. In this six-day blitzkrieg of August 2008, it lost control of two “pro-Russian” and already autonomous regions, South Ossetia and Abkhasia, which became Russian protectorates, after Russia officially recognised their independence in 2008. After two hours of intense “bartasse”, in the middle of the bushes and ferns which obstructed an old path, and with a total amazement, we were picked up by soldiers stationed there to monitor the border, about ten kilometres away as the crow flies. In 2019, the post was still in place, but empty and we had the leisure to return to survey the immense Caucasian glaciers, a stone's throw from the Russian-Georgian border. The context linked to the war in Ukraine is disrupting the destiny of Georgia, which for a time opted for European integration and which is today tossed between two paths. Its president, Salomé Zourabichvili, former French ambassador to Georgia, perfectly French-speaking and pro-European, occupies a mainly symbolic position. The party in power since 2012, “Georgian Dream”, founded by billionaire oligarch Bidzina Ivanishvili, initially claimed to be centre-left and was described as favourable to the market economy and for rapprochement with the West, became openly pro-Russian from 2021-2022. The legislative elections of 26 October 2024, considered “existential” for the future of the country, allowed this party to further strengthen its power, against a backdrop of irregularities and authoritarian excesses.
Ce contexte a menacé la faisabilité de c: This context threatened the feasibility of this trip to Georgia: on the website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Ariane), the border is now highlighted with a red border, identifying the “formally discouraged” areas. In other words, a “no go” in the context of organising a commercial trip. I had to deploy (a little) energy to finally receive the approval of the ministry and the embassy.
Mardi 2 avril, on se retrouve (presque): Tuesday 2 April, we meet (almost) all at Geneva airport. Although I know almost everyone, this is not the case for the participants. Managing a commercial trip also means trying to bring together people who are likely to find points of convergence. For this, nothing better than a journey of more than 24 hours, from Paris/Geneva to Oushgouli, in the depths of Upper Svaneti. The entire group finally meets up in the impressive grounds of Istanbul airport, and this event really marks the beginning of the trip for me, since it strongly influences the rest of the celebrations. After a night of air travel and a stopover, here we are in Tbilissi, where Guladi is already waiting for us to drive us across Georgia, aboard his old Mercedes bus. Belt behind his back, his supple behaviour is strangely not modified by his numerous phone calls, with the phone to his ear. Guladi has his addresses, and the breaks are probably not haphazard. During one of them, we eat our first khachapuri, marking for me the real return to Georgia. We are then at the beginning of the Ingouri valley, the long valley that we must go up to reach Oushgouli from Zugdidi. The Inguri hydraulic dam which stands in the middle of this valley creates a retention basin of several kilometres and contributes 40% to national energy production.
À Mestia, nous retrouvons Shako, avec qu: In Mestia, we find Shako, with whom I will work for this crossing. I only know him by reputation, and by the few phone calls we exchanged to prepare for the trip. Shako lives here, with his wife and two children. He is a IFMGA guide, like me, and a very good skier. Winner of the local stage of the Freeride World Tour Qualifier in 2023, he loves skiing and prefers not to concede skiability to the weight of the equipment. This is what surprises me when I hand his pair of skis to the driver posted on the roof of his “Delica”, these small 4x4 trucks which are legion here, essential for our transfer to Oushgouli. We arrive just in time to appreciate the fantastic sunset lights on the numerous towers of the village, at the time used as a protection bunker by each family in the event of attacks and which have become symbols of the region. The imposing wall of Chkhara emerges in fragments and gives us chills with its alpine character.
À peine le dîner commencé, Shako nous pr: As soon as dinner has started, Shako offers us a friendly drink. He goes behind the bar counter, takes out a bottle with translucent contents and pours small glasses copiously. According to him, “chacha” is enjoyed during the meal. Here, the dijo starts early! She is “strong” the chacha, and on the eve of departure for 7 days of journeying, no one dares to have more! Except Shako, of course, who happily shares a few extra drinks with the Delica drivers. They don't count the strokes before taking the steep road back to Mestia!
Oushgouli-Adishi : trois jours en cabane: Oushgouli-Adishi: three days in cabins in the shadow of Chkhara
Ce premier jour de ski en Géorgie va tei: This first day of skiing in Georgia will colour the rest of the journey. It snowed last night, like the previous days, and the wind up there didn't stop blowing. The landscape is immaculate, grandiose. But tricky, too. This morning, it almost feels like we're in an Aravis valley on a Saturday morning, as two large groups of skiers are ahead of us. They stop at the end of the first bump, a great classic of the area. We then continue to walk on a ridge which never sees skiers. As we walk three abreast, not far from the ridge, we feel a whoop followed by a continuous noise. My reflex focuses on the opposite slope but there is no trace of avalanche activity. There was definitely an avalanche, and it started right below us. A 40cm break on part of the face... first alert, I have never triggered such a slab in the Alps, and even less remotely. The fragile layer is sensitive and spreads very easily.  A few hundred metres further on, we witness a second alert, much more serious. The scenario is the same. The leading group passes without problem a few cables from the summit ridge, and it is when the second group passes that the entire face leaves, 5m below. At the highest point, the break is around a metre, it's really impressive.  I'm going to see what's underneath: the fragile layer is made up of around twenty centimeters of cups...
Nous rejoignons les deux petites cabanes: We reach the two small cabins in which we will sleep this evening. They are still under construction, and the ones we occupy are stored around twenty rolls of glass wool. The table and benches were quickly put together, using metal bed bases and scrap boards. As usual, Etienne stirs and praises the qualities of his new inflatable mattress. Until the fateful moment when, by making him move on the wooden floor, which is certainly new but not perfect, he notices that it is softening... We had a good laugh. Him less. The Chkhara finally emerges with the lights of the setting sun, it is both incredible and frightening.  And even more so when, at bedtime, its serac discharges copiously and an avalanche sweeps the entire face. The Caucasus is not the Alps, that is the main lesson from this first day of skiing.
Le créneau météo bouge tout le temps. La: The weather window changes all the time. The snow will fall in the afternoon and we get up accordingly. Soon a ray of sunshine and a few stolen photos with the Russian-Georgian border ridge in the background. With lightning speed, a cloud front invades the sky from the west. However, and as the forecasts indicated, the ceiling remains around 4000m, leaving us with the prospect of a descent via the glacier. Little slope, but a great atmosphere. The snow, excellent at the top, quickly becomes crusty. Here, the temperature gradients are significant, as evidenced by the numerous crawls. We return to our two small shepherd huts, the “Khalde mountain farms”. One is equipped with an old wood stove and three box springs revered by Pascal, Quentin and Shako who have skipped the mattresses. The other is empty, and its old parquet floor accommodates our inflatable mattresses.
La nuit a été fraîche. La neige a immacu: The night was cool. The snow has immaculately covered the slopes above us, covering areas left bare by previous avalanches. The border chain, this high wall, continues to crush us with its magnitude. From the unnamed summit that we reach, the view is striking, particularly of Tetnuldi, a peak that I had climbed when I first came to Georgia, 10 years ago. I don't know if I leave much choice to Shako, but I start the descent first, in cinematic snow. It's fluid and the small hard bottom allows you to push the turns. A delight. We all long for this descent, exclaiming with cries of joy, except perhaps Robin who throws a little too hard, jumps and lands head-to-toe. One of his skis is lost, after breaking the leash. From below, I see him coming at full speed, jumping a bump and crashing into the snow at my level. It was less a… Here, the consequences can be problematic. A long flat course of a few kilometres follows, partly pushing with sticks, partly with skins. In the distance, we see the characteristic towers of the small village of Adishi. We arrive almost on skis at the village, among the cows and via muddy paths which add to its charm (along with the towers!). Natia didn't take long to bring us eleven large beers, we needed no less to enjoy this day. Adishi is a partly ruined village, which was abandoned by its population in 1978 following a deadly winter. Shako tells us that in 2009, there were only 3 families living here and that today there are around twenty thanks to the rapid development of tourism. Moreover, as we walk above the village, we hear sounds of work coming from several homes, a sign of transformations still in progress. Aurélien, the group's winemaker, can't help but buy local wine in the village grocery store. He returns, very proud of his quest, with two plastic bottles filled with the precious liquid, one red, the other orange. Flawless wines according to him, but obviously not to everyone's taste... They go wonderfully with the many dishes that cover every square inch of the table: grated carrot salad with coriander, slices of grilled eggplant filled with fresh cheese, khachapouri with cheese and meat, chicken meat in sauce, pan-fried cauliflower. A real feast!
Groupe progressant skis aux pieds, Ushgu: Group progressing on skis, Ushguli, at the foot of Shkhara, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Skieur progressant skis aux pieds dans l: Skier progressing on skis in the valley, Ushguli and Shkhara sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Skieur descendant une grande pente poudr: Skier descending a large powdery slope, Adishi and Tetnuldi sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Bétail conduit dans une ruelle du villag: Cattle driven in a village alley, Adishi and Tetnuldi sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Il y avait plusieurs options pour cette: There were several options for the day. I was keen to climb to the shoulder of Tetnuldi and ski its glacier all the way to Mestia. But Shako says the final section, between a deep canyon and dense scrub, is too much of a struggle. As a consolation prize, I suggest that instead of taking a taxi from Zhabeshi, below the Tetnuldi ski resort, to Mestia, we make the connection on foot and on skis. On paper, almost 30 km and a little over 2000m of ascent. Much to my surprise — and delight — a good part of the team joins me. After climbing an unnamed summit at 3500m overlooking the imposing Tetnuldi glacier, we descend towards the ski resort, which was still being built when I first visited Georgia in 2014. There are plenty of descent lines on the north side, where the Freeride World Tour event takes place. Kai, the dog who has followed us since the second day, leaves us here for another group of skiers. Good powder higher up turns into wonderful corn snow lower down, just before a fairly gentle spell of bushwhacking through the Svanetian scrub. We easily reach Zhabeshi, where 3 teams emerge: team taxi, team trainers-and-running, and team walking-and-skiing. We reach Mestia at nightfall. The town is undergoing a ‘tourist’ transformation, with a very mixed collection of buildings: luxury hotels alongside makeshift constructions. People in the streets look at us as though we have emerged from another world. Without any transition, we sit down to a gargantuan meal, and as usual dishes cover the table until the tablecloth disappears. I am particularly fond of the potatoes fried in fat and the salads in which coriander reigns supreme.
Il ne fallait pas trop le chauffer. Ayan: You shouldn't heat it too much. Having had the misfortune of talking to Shako about chacha, he disappears for a moment, returning with a bottle of the beverage artisanally distilled in Svaneti. It may be artisanal, but you can feel it coming through! And for the honor, we finish the bottle. But soon comes the suggestion of a typically Georgian trap: Shako suggests that we take a “little tour of the city”, in other words, have an excess of chacha… He therefore leads us to a small, rather trendy bar in the city, which also happens to be the haunt of the Mestia guides. One of them, who does not really have the morphotype of the guide, is quickly presented to us. The “bear”, as we will call him for his physique and his teddy bear look, holds in his hand a small goat's horn which he distributes to anyone who comes to him, having previously taken care to fill it to the brim with the precious translucent remedy. This chacha is of his own production, it is as busy as the previous one, but does not raise any Georgian eyebrows. The local police car, gyro on, is camped in front of the bar, but that does not prevent a small group from smoking large stalks of marijuana, or from taking the car parked in front of the bar, apparently above the legal limit of 0g/L. Here, the relationship with the rules seems more flexible than at home! Special mention to Aurélien who missed the first train and who joined us by chance, opening the door of the first bar found on the way when leaving the guest house. And to Arthur, our evening animal, who was given a no go by a Georgian, finding that he was approaching, although in a non-offensive way, a group of Georgians, making himself understood by materializing the “red line”.
Skieurs suivant la trace sur une crête a: Skiers following the track on an aerial ridge, Adishi and Tetnuldi sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Village et tours médiévales éclairés à l: Village and medieval towers lit up at nightfall, Mestia sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Mestia - Iskari : à l’ombre de l’Ushba: Mestia - Iskari: in the shadow of the Ushba
La “Cloud base hut” est une cabane non-g: The “Cloud base hut” is an unguarded hut owned by Nick, another Mestia guide. In Svaneti, as long as you own land, have been “from here” for several generations and respect the local architectural style thanks to the use of wood, it is allowed to build your own cabin. Shako, who owns land a little above, thinks about it. Great friend of Nick, they had organised a big inauguration drinking party, as the Georgians have the secret, 8 years ago, then joining the cabin in a 4x4 on a dry track. Except that it snowed 50cm during the night. They then took a whole day to manage to get the cars back down... This morning, the group is silent, everyone busy sweating out the excesses of the day before. The characteristic roof of the cabin finally appears, the longest day for some, the shortest on the map. Of the chacha adventurers of the day before, only Shako seems to suffer nothing. And yet, the horn has satisfied him much more often than us! He is busy organising life in the cabin and soon, cooking us a feast on the stove. The pasta is certainly not al dente, but subtly seasoned in the Georgian style. This evening, the local cognac that Shako made is not very successful...
Maisons de svanétie dominées par les ver: Svaneti houses dominated by snow-covered slopes, Mestia sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Bâtiment de montagne au milieu d’un vast: Mountain building in the middle of a vast snow cover, Mestia sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
5h, le réveil met en branle la maisonnée: 5am, and the alarm wakes the household. Shako has prepared another feast: a generous omelette with all the extras, and porridge. We have barely left the hut when we spot an animal running in the distance, the first of the trip. Wolf or fox? Shako’s money is on the former. Sunrise facing Ushba’s imposing east face is fantastic. On the other side, the Leïla Peak range gives me ideas for another visit. The descent of the Chaalali glacier is disappointing: since our first days, the snow has begun to change, developing a thin refrozen crust that is rather unsettling to ski. We make up for it on the SE face, where the corn snow is particularly good and invites great sweeping turns at full speed! By lunchtime, the snow has become sticky and deep. Now we are losing height more than skiing, and it all ends on foot, through the muddy streets of the small hamlet of Mazeri. We pass oxen pulling a little trailer full of manure, a couple busy steering the animals while spreading its contents evenly into furrows dug beforehand. We also pass the ‘Mazeri ski resort’, a small drag lift for the village ‘kids’. The grand Ushba hotel, our resting place for the night, was designed by Shako for his final-year project: before becoming an IFMGA guide, Shako was a civil engineer.
Skieur progressant sur le fil d’une crêt: Skier progressing along the edge of a ridge, Mestia sector, during a ski traverse in Upper Svaneti.
Il faut s'y résoudre, nous arrivons au t: We have to resolve it, we are reaching the end of this incredible adventure. We have one step left to reach our final village: Iskari and complete a beautiful route crossing upper Svaneti from one side to the other. A long step to reach Mt Bak. In the forest above Mazeri, we follow old ski tracks, and soon huge marks in the snow: this time, there is no doubt about the animal that passed by, we come face to face with bear tracks. Shako has already seen it several times, including recently at the base camp of Leïla Peak, the flagship summit of the mountain range which sets the scene for the south of the valley that we have been “descending” for 7 days. Besides, I've been eyeing this chain since we left, with the crazy desire to cross it on skis one day. We are soon out of the woods. That's it, it's spring. I replace the ski trousers with shorts. Access to Bok Pass is much longer than I imagined. All of a sudden, two beautiful grouse that we had been hearing for a while take flight. Although protected, these animals are poached in Svaneti. This last climb is still putting a strain on bodies that have already been under strain in recent days, even if they are now better accustomed to long-term effort. A collective photo at the top of Mount Bok then we engage in large curves in its broad southern slopes. The snow becomes softer and softer, and we soon have to battle with the bushes before finding ourselves in meadows dotted with patches of snow, now a minority. The most daring prepare for the “skiing of tomorrow”, sometimes fatal for the edges. And at some point, you have to decide to change your outfit.
Après avoir traversé la rue en terre bat: After crossing the dirt street through the small village of Iskari, we arrive in an interior courtyard where a mobile sawmill has just been used which is not new. The blade is missing teeth and there is obviously no protection. Moreover, our host has a finger wrapped in a large bandage, and when I ask him the cause of this injury, he points to the saw. They are busy cleaning the sawdust meticulously. Then, the cows are returned to a particularly well-kept stable. While surveying the premises, we came across a dirt room warmed by the purring of around ten servers. Our host, a farmer like everyone else in these small, remote villages, mines bitcoins. These people will never cease to surprise us with their ingenuity and resourcefulness, behind an image that we could too quickly attach to them. Here, everything is very clean and well kept. The only shower is very hot. The women are very discreet and little (or not at all) smiling. On the other hand, mischief can be seen in the eyes of our host, who does not take long to bring us a first bottle of chacha arranged, half cognac, half chacha, following the welcome lunch he offers us upon our arrival. Lunch as much as chacha are totems of Svanetian welcome and for no reason would they refuse each other. Except that it's only 15:00, and at the rate that the glasses are emptying then refilling, either the chacha will quickly run out of stock, or it's our ability to absorb the alcohol that will be lacking. Obviously, there is never a shortage of chacha... Our host, who recently underwent an operation, is (supposedly) forbidden from alcohol, but he seems to take a perverse pleasure in making us drink by proxy!
Après sept jours à partager le quotidien: After seven days of sharing the daily life of this crazy adventure, and gradually discovering this man with a discreet approach, we must realise that we must greet our local guide, a fine connoisseur of his mountains and traditions. The emotion is palpable and it is shared. But quickly, the call of the chacha takes over: the bottle of arranged chacha is finished, now it's time for the pitchers of pure chacha. The state of my companions quickly declines, as for me, who does not want to repeat the experience of Mestia, I only honor with measure the immeasurable generosity of our host. At the table, the atmosphere is joyful, and Arthur, as a good evening captain, leads us through the meal with a one-man show of which he alone has the secret...

Ski en Grèce : traversée du Tzoumerka et: Skiing in Greece: crossing the Tzoumerka and the Pindos
Sept jours de traversée à ski en Grèce,: Seven days of ski traverse in Greece, from Tzoumerka to Pindos: stone villages, century-old pines and the summit of Smolikas.
Deux skieurs de randonnée sur une crête: Two ski tourers on a snowy ridge, large mountain landscape, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Skier en Grèce. Dans l'imaginaire collec: Skiing in Greece. In the collective imagination, it is neither a country of snow nor a country of skiing. This is precisely why I wanted to go there: for the improbable, the unexpected and the doubts.
Nous avons choisi de rejoindre l'Épire s: We chose to reach Epirus without a plane, by train then by ferry. Then come the Tzoumerka, steep and mineral, its stone villages and its hanging monasteries, then the Pindos, gentler, with their long ridges and their century-old pines. Seven days of crossing to Smolikas, the second highest peak in Greece, for a journey about which, just a few days before departure, I was sure of almost nothing.
Groupe en traversee, pinde — smolikas et: Group crossing, pinde — smolikas and pades, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Une traversée des montagnes de l'Épire,: A crossing of the mountains of Epirus, from the mineral reliefs of Tzoumerka to the long wooded ridges of Pindos, to the second highest peak in Greece.
Passage par Nereda et Matsouki avant de: Passage through Nereda and Matsouki before reaching the village of Kalarites on foot.
Col Baros, sommet du Kalogiros puis Souf: Baros Pass, summit of Kalogiros then Souflomiti SE, before the descent to Matsouki.
Traversée par le lac Noss et le massif d: Crossing Lake Noss and the Balcaz massif, then long descent to Anthochori.
Entrée dans les Pindes par les longues c: Entrance into the Pindos via the long ridges of the Valia Kalda, between beech forests, century-old pines and rounded peaks.
Longue traversée de crêtes jusqu'à la st: Long crossing of ridges to the Vasilitsa station, following the areas still covered in snow.
Crêtes sommitales, chapelles orthodoxes: Summit ridges, Orthodox chapels and long descents between the pines before reaching Samarina.
Ascension du Smolikas, deuxième sommet d: Ascent of Smolikas, the second highest peak in Greece, then final descent towards Pades to complete the crossing.
Le voyage commence avant les skis: The journey begins before the skis
4h, le réveil sonne. Je sais que la jour: 4 a.m., the alarm rings. I know it's going to be a long day because to get to Greece, we chose not to take the plane. Not taking a plane means combining several modes of transport. First go to Novara by car, and leave the car there to take a first train then a second train to Brindisi, in Puglia, in the very south of Italy. Then, if all goes well, we will board a ferry which, during the night, will take us to Igoumenitsa, a Greek port located in the northwest, in the region of Epirus.
De là, encore quelques heures de taxi, e: From there, a few more hours by taxi, and we will finally be able to put on skis, in the south of the Tzoumerka massif, located to the south of the Pindes massif.
Évidemment, tout ne se passe pas comme p: Obviously, everything doesn't go as planned. We had planned to leave with Aurélien's car, an old Scénic from the early 2000s. But after a few kilometres, it faulted. We pick up Aurélien, leave his car there, and finally leave with Osman's.
À quelques kilomètres du Tunnel du Mont-: A few kilometres from the Mont-Blanc Tunnel, a notice board indicates: “Tunnel access road closed, avalanche shooting”. It snowed last night, once again, and the risk of avalanches in the French Alps is maximum. New cold sweat at the idea of ​​not keeping the schedules. After a few minutes of waiting, the line of cars starts moving again. The barriers rise, traffic resumes, and we pass without incident.
À Novara, le petit parking que j'utilise: In Novara, the small car park I usually use is full. Another uncertainty. We end up finding a place to leave the car. Regional train to Milan. Three takeaway pizzas from a bad pizzeria near Milan Central Station. Then we look up at the building, massive, monumental, almost overwhelming. A stone architecture that imposes more than it welcomes.
Sept heures de train jusqu'au sud de l'I: Seven hours by train to southern Italy. I'm jubilant. I like this slow way of travelling.
In Rimini the train stops. A long time. Then a message: for reasons of judicial investigation, traffic is interrupted for two hours. Someone threw themselves under the previous train — rest their soul — but, for us, that complicates everything. Quick calculation: it's going to be tight.
Le train repart. J'espère encore. Un app: The train leaves. I still hope. A call to the ferry company puts an end to the illusion: you have to be there at least an hour before departure. With our delay, it's impossible.
Je réserve un hôtel à Brindisi. Je réorg: I book a hotel in Brindisi. I'm reorganizing. I inform the group. I book them a taxi so that they can reach the start of the first stage without us.
Le lendemain matin, nous profitons de ce: The next morning, we took advantage of this forced stopover to visit Brindisi a little. Then head to the port, after buying some rusticos and pasticciotti. The crossing takes place on rough seas. Given the expected arrival time and the three-hour drive to Tzoumerka, I decide to sleep in Igoumenitsa.
Départ avant l'aube le lendemain pour re: Departure before dawn the next day to join the clients and attack the first stage of our crossing of the Tzoumerka. More than 2000 metres of altitude difference. Objective: Matsouki, then on foot, skis on your back, Kalarites.
Depuis plusieurs jours, je doute de l'en: For several days, I have doubts about the snowfall. Impossible to clearly read the boundary on satellite images. This first step is decisive. I only reserved this first part; the rest remains conditional.
7 h. Refuge Stavros. Petite cahute perch: 7 a.m. Stavros Shelter. Small perched hut, view overlooking the valley. Reunion with the group.
À Nereda, aucune âme qui vive. Vers 1500: In Nereda, not a single living soul. Around 1500 metres, facing south, we put on our skis. Good sign.
Le ciel annoncé dégagé se referme rapide: The forecasted clear sky closes quickly. Fog. First pass, then second, without visibility, barely the tips of the spatulas. Then the clouds part. Light. Easy snow. Great curves. At 1500 metres, the snow ends, both in the north and in the south. Odd.
Longue marche jusqu'à Matsouki. Un ancie: Long walk to Matsouki. An elder greets us. In the square, a big fire: it is the period of Apokries, the Greek carnival preceding Lent. Costumes, music, fire in front of the chapel.
Sentier pavé, monastère suspendu au-dess: Paved path, monastery suspended above the valley. Then descent towards Kalarites.
19 h. Première bière. Quatre heures de m: 19:00 First beer. Four hours of walking with skis on your back.
Depart a pied en foret, tzoumerka — sect: Departure on foot in the forest, tzoumerka - theodoriana sector, during a ski journey in Greece.
Traversee a ski sur neige, tzoumerka — s: Ski traverse on snow, tzoumerka — theodoriana sector, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Nous dormons chez Napoléon Zaglis. Un ho: We sleep at Napoléon Zaglis’s house. A man who must probably be in his seventh decade, with a stocky figure, with his laughing eyes and his thick mustache that marks his face. With his wife, they run a restaurant-grocery store and a few rooms. From the outset, we felt a warm welcome, from them and from their employee, who also had a laughing look. When Thomas asks him for “Isabella” wine, a marketed and conventionally produced wine, his reaction is immediate: “we don't have this wine, it's illegal to serve that!” ". All this to say that at Napoléon, only good products come in!
Les plats s'enchaînent, et la table est: The dishes follow one another, and the table is soon covered with garnished plates: Greek salad, seasonal salad, meats of all kinds, cheese.
Sur la place, la fête continue. Un immen: In the square, the party continues. A huge blaze, the name of the village cut out in large letters in front of the flames. Traditional music rises: almost oriental sounds, catchy, hypnotic. Greeks extend their hands to us and we soon form a circle. We are caught up in the dance. Hand in hand, we circle around the fire. We are handed a glass, a plate. Impossible to refuse.
Décidément, ces Grecs ont l'âme généreus: Clearly, these Greeks have generous souls.
La chambre est dominée par de vieilles b: The room is dominated by old dark woodwork, weathered by time. Wood frames the windows, clads the walls, makes up the headboard. A light smell of resin still floats. Simple, massive furniture. Nothing superfluous. We feel the mountains and past winters.
Ce matin, c'est la femme de Napoléon qui: This morning, it is Napoleon's wife who serves us breakfast, and when her husband arrives in the room, we feel that love among them does not erode over the years.
Village de montagne, tzoumerka — secteur: Mountain village, tzoumerka — theodoriana sector, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Nous repartons sur la route goudronnée q: We set off again on the asphalt road which goes up to the Baros pass, then we leave it for a path which soon gets lost in the bushes. The shortcut isn't saving us any time this morning. We emerge on a small promontory, where a chapel dominates the entire valley. We are ringing the bell! Like the day before, we climb to 1500 m, then go up a rounded ridge to the summit of Kalogiros (2088 m).
Aujourd'hui, nous avons peu de distance: Today, we have little effective distance, so we take the opportunity to do a little skiing. The snow is particularly good, a small layer of powder on top of a hard bottom. And safe!
Nous redescendons la grande pente Est du: We go back down the large eastern slope of Kalogiros, then go back up to Souflomiti SE. The next two valleys, due north, delight us. I was afraid that the snow had started to transform in the north, but that this transformation would be partial and that we would be skiing bad crusty snow. But there were two days of good weather the previous week, then another small snowfall the day before our arrival, stabilizing the snow conditions and making skiing pleasant! And despite the heat, this powder doesn't move, surprisingly!
Après avoir pas mal porté les skis les d: After having carried the skis quite a bit the previous two days, this time we went down and back up on foot in the same valley. So we literally empty our bags and head along a forest track to the village of Matsouki, reached just as the public lighting begins to illuminate the stone streets. A sign reads “La Verliga, radio”. Christos Zacharis, the owner of the bar-restaurant of the same name, is also a journalist and host of this web radio, in the Aspropotami and Vlach languages.
