Nous pénétrons dans une pièce sombre, éc: We enter a dark room, lit by fairy lights, and with a stone slab floor. A big white dog sits there, in the middle of the tables. The benches are covered with long-haired fabrics, customary for these places. The beers are followed by numerous dishes, always very salty (as is often the case here!): tomato salad, meatballs, beef and pork, pieces of lamb, cheese...
Puis arrive le moment d'aller au lit. Th: Then it's time to go to bed. Thomas, who had spoken with Christos, seems to say that we are going to sleep in different houses in the village.
Aux questions pressantes et un brin inqu: To Amélie's pressing and slightly worried questions, Christos shows us the different benches that cover the entire walls of his restaurant. Benches around thirty centimeters wide, on which small moss and these famous long-haired blankets are placed. We think he's joking. But quickly we understand that we will have to sleep in this room.
Chacun à notre tour, nous testons les ba: We each take turns testing the benches. They are really narrow and the little foam is very fine; it does not completely absorb the hardness of wooden benches. So we are reorganizing the restaurant room. We push the tables and install these little moss on the ground, a layer of moss on the stones that make up the floor, and the long-haired blanket on top. Four small foams in width, approximately 1.20 m, constitute a double bed.
Nous nous installons tout autour du poêl: We sit around the stove and Thomas and Mathieu will work all night loading it so that it continues to heat us.
La nuit n'a pas été si mauvaise, enfin p: The night wasn't so bad, well maybe not for everyone. Christos' big white dog slept with us and, excited in the early morning, rubs against each of us as a morning greeting.
Diner en refuge, tzoumerka — vallée de m: Dinner in a hut, tzoumerka — matsouki valley, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Nous remontons jusqu'au petit col, mais: We go up to the small pass, but when we get there, Aurélien has disappeared. He followed me though. The group had stretched out a little, each walking at their own pace on this trail covered the day before. The minutes pass and Aurélien does not show up. Surprising without really being so. We know Aurélien, quick to lose his things and sometimes to lose himself. It’s Aurèle, he’s like that, and we adore him like that.
Au bout d'une demi-heure, je me résous à: After half an hour, I decide to call him. He has already climbed up to the snow twice without finding us. I send him my location on WhatsApp, tell him to turn on Google Maps, and soon he's back on the right path.
Le chien de Christos nous a suivis. Il s: Christos' dog followed us. He seems happy in the snow, covering three times the distance we cover. But the gusts of wind sting his eyes and whip his whiskers.
Du col, nous basculons par une combe un: From the pass, we go through a somewhat steep valley then go up to the summit of Lake Noss, the highest point in the north of the Balcaz massif. Some steep passages complicate the dog's progress. I would prefer him to return to the village rather than to fall with us. A crossing that is too steep will destroy its capabilities on frozen snow. We lose him here, hoping he comes back down to his master.
De l'autre côté, une belle combe nous of: On the other side, a beautiful valley offers us delicious snow to ski. But around 1500 metres, you already have to put your sneakers back on. A path not indicated on the map takes us back to Anthochori, the last stop in this wild massif and ideal for skiing. In three days, we didn't come across anyone, only a trace of a snowshoe.
Hélène nous accueille chaleureusement. T: Hélène welcomes us warmly. Three bedrooms: two for couples, one for singles. She is not normally allowed to cook for customers, but due to the lack of an accessible restaurant, she prepares us a meal, asking us to remain discreet. She seems happy to let us taste a local specialty.
Plus tard, nous traversons la route pour: Later, we cross the road to go for a drink. A stove sits in the middle of the room with long horizontal tubing and 90-degree elbows that would make French standards falter. Here, we keep the heat in. Behind us, some elders are smoking. When we return, our clothes smell strongly of cigarettes.
Un message à Christos : son chien n'est: A message to Christos: his dog still hasn't come home. This worries us. Had we made the right choice?
Le lendemain, nous partons vers les Pind: The next day, we leave for Pindos. The relief is gentler than in Tzoumerka: rounded mountains, endless ridges. Copernicus satellite images make me change the route to avoid a snow-free area. We advance from ridge to ridge.
Les hêtres dominent d'abord, puis plus h: The beech trees dominate at first, then higher up the twisted pines appear. Most are headless, they have lost their heads, sculpted by the storms. These pines are majestic.
Après près de 2000 mètres de dénivelé, l: After almost 2000 metres of altitude difference, the sun sets. We decide to go to the top for bed. Up there, a small white chapel and, as far as the eye can see, the Greek mountains bathed in orange light. It's cold but the beauty of the moment makes us forget it.
La descente est incroyable : quelques ce: The descent is incredible: a few centimeters of powder on a hard bottom, smooth terrain, then a dense beech forest.
Nous sommes récupérés au col pour éviter: We are picked up at the pass to avoid the long asphalt road to Périvoli. Running downhill, at night, with the lights of the village in the background.
Dans la grande salle vitrée du restauran: In the large glass room of the restaurant, two stoves heat the room. More dogs. The meal arrives: tzatziki, Greek salads, meat in sauce with rice. Perhaps the best cuisine of the stay.
La tenancière nous raconte leur vie ici,: The owner tells us about their life here, seven months a year in the village. Everything was built by her and her husband. Their passion became their job. She speaks with pride about Valia Kalda and her attachment to the territory.
Pins tortures dans la neige, pinde — pér: Pines tortured in the snow, pinde — perivoli and vasilitsa, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Chapelle givree au crepuscule, pinde — p: Frosty chapel at dusk, pindus — perivoli and vasilitsa, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Le lendemain, longue crête pour relier P: The next day, long ridge to connect Périvoli to Vasilitsa, the only passage still covered in snow. A small northern valley offers us a few bends before an endless climb towards the summit above the station. From there, we easily reach the pass and the station.
J'avais initialement réservé à Smixi, ma: I had originally booked in Smixi, but Yanis' injury complicated the logistics. Finally, we sleep at Vasilitsa 1850, a hybrid between resort hotel and hut, in a dormitory.
Le système de restauration est particuli: The catering system is special. You have to choose carefully: excellent bean soup, good veal with tomato-lemon sauce, uneven burgers. However, several of us were delighted to return, for one evening, to our Western dishes.
Yanis est très sympa, il a vécu à Chamon: Yanis is very nice, he lived in Chamonix during Covid. Panos seems gruff, but we won't stop at that first impression.
Vue vers les vallees, pinde — périvoli e: View towards the valleys, pinde — perivoli and vasilitsa, during a ski journeying in Greece.
Ici, nous sommes loin du refuge de monta: Here, we are far from the mountain hut where the conditions of the mountain guide the waking time. Here, we have to deal with the pace of the ski resort, and there is no possibility of breakfast before 8 a.m. And always this weird order-taking system, à la carte but where the menu is only available from the mouth of the owner. Fortunately the day is short and we are not in too much of a hurry. Ultimately, this “transition” day will be longer than expected!
La première montée se termine sur une ma: The first climb ends on a magnificent corniced ridge, which allows us to reach these small Orthodox chapels typical of certain Greek summits, modest constructions dedicated to a saint and often erected at the highest point, as a discreet sign of the link between the mountain and the sacred. The descent, on perfectly spring snow, turns into a slalom test between the pines, which are more or less densely planted. I understand from the excitement of my companions that they want more. So we go back to the summit in the blazing heat.
De là, deux options s'offraient à moi :: From there, two options were available to me: either respect the line drawn the day before, which seemed to be optimized to prolong the slide as much as possible based on the latest satellite photos of the massif, or let yourself be caught up in the slope, and then take notice. Obviously, the second option quickly won out, plunging us into an awkward situation. A good quagmire in prospect, unless you cross a hilly and tortured slope on the side. Scratching won't be enough, and we'll have to re-skin, causing some protests within the group! Fortunately, a picnic spot overlooking the valley awaited us at the summit!
La suite de la descente n'est pas plus r: The rest of the descent is no smoother, and we quickly give up. Swapping skis for sneakers doesn't help us, however. The path is below but a section of dense and steep forest separates us from it. I am not unhappy to find the yellow dots, surrounded by a red circle, which mark the paths here. We join a path on the mountainside, traced among century-old pines. At a quarry, one of them, enormous, even stands on two legs, perhaps resulting from the fusion of two pine trees.
Depuis le début de notre séjour ici, nou: Since the beginning of our stay here, we have noted with desolation the consequences of the autumn floods, which ravaged Epirus. Here, the bridge which was to allow us to cross the river has disappeared, forcing us to test, at least in part, its temperature.
Nous arrivons enfin au monastère, celui-: We finally arrive at the monastery, the same one that seemed so close to us a few hours earlier. From there, two teams are formed: those that our host comes to pick up by car, and those who walk, or run, without their backpacks.

Nous arrivons à Samarina, village assez: We arrive in Samarina, a fairly large village, where most of the houses have their shutters closed. Right next to the Guest House, a large building covered in red steel appears to be a church. There, on the roof of a small annex, a large pine tree grows, symbol of this massif where this tree grows supreme. An old black and white photo, probably on film, shows this same tree and priests in cassocks. Surprisingly, it does not seem to have grown that much since this period, perhaps revealing the slow growth of these trees, some of which must be several hundred years old. The owners of the Guest House also run a restaurant downtown, where they accommodated us for dinner.
Paradoxalement, le centre de Samarina es: Paradoxically, the centre of Samarina is lively. Several restaurants surround the central square. Fortunately Mike comes to meet us, because we could have quite easily entered the wrong address. At the entrance to his tavern, a lamb butchered and hung by its back legs provides the framework for what is offered on the menu! A priori, we are going to eat meat this evening. We give Mike carte blanche, and soon the table is covered with many dishes, so that the tablecloth becomes invisible. Tripe, lamb, beef and pork, and a few side dishes, incidentally.
Pour la première fois depuis le début de: For the first time since the start of the crossing, a real wine list will allow us to discover this element of Greek culture. We compare Pinot Noir and Tannat, grape varieties quite widespread in Europe, with Xinomavro, an indigenous grape variety which enhances a wine produced biodynamically. A favourite for the team, and first of all for our demanding winemaker!
Ambiance urbaine, pinde — vasilitsa et s: Urban atmosphere, pinde — vasilitsa and samarina, during a ski journey in Greece.
Dernier jour, et non des moindres, puisq: Last day, and not the least, since we plan the ascent of the second highest peak in Greece, Smolikas. For once, we insist a little more than usual to be able to have an early breakfast. I told Panagiotis that we will be at 15:00 at the meeting point, on the other side of the Smolikas.
Samarina est relativement élevé et, à pr: Samarina is relatively high and, at almost 1500 metres above sea level, this village offers us the possibility of leaving almost on skis.
Le Smolikas se présente comme une longue: The Smolikas appears as a long summit ridge, punctuated by several successive peaks. The game of the day will consist of scraping as much snow as possible to avoid covering these distances on foot. So, as soon as we reach a high point and a slope lends itself to a very rapid descent, we let ourselves slide to reach the next summit.
À la fin, à quelques encablures du point: At the end, a short distance from the highest point of the ridge, the spring snow is so good that the scraping turns into a beautiful descent. A descent that we will pay for at the price of the difference in altitude to go back up, but that is the game of the ski touring.
Et voilà, nous sommes tous réunis au som: And there we are, we are all gathered at the summit, at the summit of this week-long crossing through the Epirus Mountains, an incredible crossing. I wasn't sure of anything when I plotted this route, and I was even less sure a few days before departure when I saw the snow line so high.
C'est sûrement le voyage qui m'a demandé: This is probably the trip that required the most preparation, both because the Greeks have this annoying tendency to not respond to messages when they use encrypted messaging, and because, for many others, it is almost impossible to reach them other than by phone or SMS.
D'ici, nous voyons notre point de départ: From here, we see our starting point: Kakarditsa, the highest point of the Tzoumerka massif, at the foot of which we passed a few days earlier. It seems far, immensely far. And then, a little closer, these rounded mountains which mark the southern entrance to the Pindes massif.
Reste la descente, qui encore une fois n: There remains the descent, which once again does not seem entirely obvious. The game, as from the beginning of this trip, consists of optimizing the snow limit as much as possible, scraping the snow where it remains and skiing down almost at all costs.
Mais à ce jeu-là, nous ne gagnons jamais: But in this game, we never win below 1500 metres of altitude. It is by a path evolving through southern vegetation that we finish this beautiful crossing, and find Panagiotis in the village of Pades.
Nous déposons nos compagnons du sud-oues: We drop off our companions from the southwest in Ioannina, with a quick goodbye in view of these good times shared.

Itinérance à ski dans les montagnes sauv: Journeying on skis in the wild mountains of Kazakhstan
À travers les hautes vallées glaciaires: Through the high glacial valleys of Kazakhstan, the mountain guide Yann Borgnet retraces its ski traverse of the Ile Alatau mountains. Unusual encounters, big peaks and little orange huts, and an incident that could have gone wrong: here is the story of a great adventure at ski touring in the heart of Central Asia.
Mon voisin de rang est togolais, expatri: My next-door neighbour is Togolese, expatriated in Burkina Faso, in Ouagadugu. He is a researcher in sanitation systems in developing countries. There is still something intriguing about this mode of air transport, which, with its connections and connections, brings together people from incredibly varied backgrounds.
À ses yeux, je suis sportif, un grand ma: In his eyes, I am sporty, a big patient when I tell him about our project in Kazakhstan. If I had met him on the return flight, I would have told him straight away that this trip was not easy.
De Chimbulak au premier algeco: From Chimbulak to the first algeco
La station de ski de Chimbulak ne nous d: The Chimbulak ski resort does not disorient us, or at least not in the way one might imagine a post-Soviet country. Below, a row of brand-new businesses, photographers who target well-dressed tourists, young women disguised as cosmonauts who try to sell I don't know what to passers-by and large sedans - of course, electric and from unknown Chinese brands.
Au sommet des remontées mécaniques, des: At the top of the ski lifts, drones fly over the crowds of tourists coming from the city to capture the “Instagramability” of the moment, in front of a “Rolex” four by three. It’s not really the mountain that motivated us to come this far, and yet it is here that our adventure begins, the antithesis of this commodified vision.
Nous remontons une raide pente froide, c: We go up a steep cold slope, like an introduction to Kazakh snow science, to a pass topped by a slender gendarme. On the other side, the very rocky southern slope is bare, but the view of the Tuyuk-Su basin gives us the measure of the Kazakh mountains.
Au loin, nous apercevons notre premier b: In the distance, we see our first bivouac: an orange algeco inside which there are three berths, a table, a non-functional electricity production system and a stove. Aurélien (Lurquin) brought us a bottle of pinot. A large champagne to celebrate a smooth departure, enjoyed in a small stainless steel bowl found on site; here, you don’t need Zalto to appreciate it!
Scène de voyage et de ski de randonnée p: Travel scene and ski touring during the ski traverse of the Alatau Island massif, Kazakhstan, on day 1 of journeying.
La seconde journée doit nous permettre d: The second day should allow us to move into the Talgar valley, a very long valley where retreat from below would be particularly complicated. We go up to the Tuyuk-Su pass (4015 m) and take a foothold on a large corniced ridge, from which a new section of massif opens up. More rounded mountains, topped with vast bare slopes where black ice surfaces. At the bottom of the first valley, we reach a vast glacial basin.
Comme souvent dans ces configurations, i: As is often the case in these configurations, you have to aim for the banks to find skiable canyons. To the left, the south slope, completely cleared of snow, is home to a flock of birds that fly away as we pass.
Notre bivouac est le même que la veille,: Our bivouac is the same as the day before, an orange algeco with basic equipment. It is only midday and we have the afternoon to enjoy the silence of this place, cut off from the world, without network or human trace. The most remote point of our crossing.
Le contour des montagnes s’irrise déjà d: The outline of the mountains is already tinged with a fine white border, a sign that daybreak is near. Visually, it is really not easy to find the key to the labyrinth caused by the moraine debris. These erratic screes require us to make twists and turns, but there is just enough snow to keep our skis on. I love these situations of perpetual betting on what happens next.
Le bassin glaciaire que nous rejoignons: The glacial basin that we reach after passing the clue is vast and topped with impressive glacial peaks, distant and inaccessible. It’s incredible in its immensity and beauty, and I immortalize the moment in a frenzy.
Tout à coup, un écriteau s’affiche sur m: Suddenly, a sign appears on my screen: “unable to save file”… My SD card is dead, and there will be no way to replace it until the Cosmo station, at the very least. A blow to morale.
Scène de voyage et de ski de randonnée p: Travel scene and ski touring during the ski traverse of the Alatau Island massif, Kazakhstan, on day 2 of journeying.
Nous continuons à remonter le glacier so: We continue to go up the glacier in heavy heat. I want to reach a summit on the border with Kyrgyzstan, which would then allow us to switch to a slope that is a priori skiable. But everything is not as simple as on my map and the identified edge, initially comfortable, becomes more tapered and technical. The group's fatigue means it is necessary to recompose the initial plan and cross on the side to the west pass of the said summit.
Nous rejoignons une selle confortable, e: We reach a comfortable saddle, and, while my companions put on their skis, I set off to reconnoiter. I cross sideways in powder snow, I am relaxed. I reach a small ridge which cuts the slope vertically and marks a change in orientation.
Sans me méfier, j’engage le ski amont da: Without being suspicious, I engage the uphill ski in harder snow whose grip seems secure to me. But my downhill ski doesn't bite when I transfer my weight to it. It pulls me along, as if following a step into the void.
Mes skis grattent alors la surface de la: My skis then scrape the surface of the snow, discovering blue ice. I feel its small reliefs on my posterior buttocks. I scream. It's endless. I see everything and first of all this protruding stone towards which I am heading at full speed. I try to slow myself down by all means but obviously there is nothing I can do. Just wait and hope you don't hit too hard.
Dans ma tentative de résistance à la gra: In my attempt to resist gravity, I began to spin head first. Between the approach to the stone and my stop, a few dozen metres further, is the black hole. I stopped because the slope was getting gentler and the snow was cold and soft. I look up towards the source of my fall.
La pente de glace était en fait très rai: The icy slope was in fact very steep. But in the flat light I had seen nothing, nor felt anything through my skis. Nothing. There is blood in the snow, and I try to work out where it is coming from. My nose is fine. My lips are burning. Most worrying, though, is the pain I can feel in my thigh. I inspect my trousers without noticing anything at first. But they are torn, and the opening matches the rounded corner of my avalanche transceiver. A hole punch could not have been more precise.
Ma jambe est douloureuse et ma crainte p: My leg is painful and my main fear concerns the femur. If something were ever broken, the situation would become extremely tense. On the one hand because we are very isolated, far from everything, and on the other hand because the bad weather is arriving. I am distracted, incapable of making the slightest decision.
Une tête émerge de la crête piégeuse. C’: A head emerges from the tricky ridge. It was Thomas, who heard me scream and who immediately understood that I had fallen. Despite the shock of emotion, I am now concerned about how the group will be able to reach me safely. My companions join me by going around the ice slope, crampons on their feet.
Visiblement, Amélie est sous le choc de: Obviously, Amélie is in shock at what has just happened. The hardest part remains to be done: making a decision to cross this damn ridge safely. I have a hard time understanding the map, and the satellite images don't help me much either.
D’ici, je distingue clairement une pente: From here, I can clearly see an obvious slope to go up, but what will we find behind it? I feel that I no longer have much energy to manage the group whereas usually, such situations of uncertainty would make me jubilant.
Quelques conversions plus haut, j’attein: A few kick turns higher, I reach the pass. My first look at the far side confirms my fears. As usual, I run through the kaleidoscope of options before choosing the ‘least bad’. Following the ridge south looks difficult to manage: part of the group is already very tired, and the pain in my thigh is still sharp.
Tout droit en dessous, c’est beaucoup tr: Straight below is much too steep and steep. On the other hand, slightly below, to the right, a snow slope seems skiable. “Seems” because in the meantime, snow started to fall and visibility deteriorated considerably. What the aerial images confirm: in summer, there is a scree there. And in accordance with the laws of gravity, a scree is never very steep.
Je sors la corde pour assurer l’entrée d: I take out the rope to secure the entrance to the slope and the first turns confirm my bet, bingo! We soon set foot on the immense Gorodetsky glacier and I am now very focused on finding the best “gravity” line in this particularly tortured terrain.
Je compare la carte imprécise aux images: I compare the imprecise map to aerial images, which are more faithful to the terrain and which make it possible in particular to detect river beds. Visibility is zero and the terrain is particularly complex and tortured, but the cabin is finally reached, with more ease than I feared.
Mon bon Aurélien, fidèle parmi les fidèl: My good Aurélien, faithful among the faithful, willingly accepts the chore of filling the water cow in the stream adjoining the cabin. But when he returns, with his optimistic face that he rarely leaves, he accompanies the removal of the can with a sentence of which he keeps the secret: “nice piss! » Indeed, the water is yellowish, muddy.
Une fois que tout le monde s’est mis au: Once everyone is dry, we set about cleaning the bivouac, using the now proven technique: several bags of snow are dumped on the ground, wet and muddy, then removed with a rudimentary broom found on site. But the atmosphere remains humid: the ventilation grille has been blocked with a plastic bag, water oozes onto the window and the floor does not dry...
Au lit, il me faut trouver les positions: In bed, I have to find the least uncomfortable positions, because in addition to my right thigh, I realise that my left buttocks are also painful under pressure.
Cosmo et fin de la traversée: Cosmo and end of the crossing
Cosmo est une station d’observation astr: Cosmo is an astronomical observation station perched at 3,300m and with two Gamma telescopes still in operation, allowing cosmic rays to be analysed. This place historically depends on the Lebedev Institute of Physics of the Moscow Faculty of Sciences, which also manages two other similar bases: the station on Mount Aragats in Armenia, and another located on the Fedchenko plateau in the Pamir Mountains, in Tajikistan.
Ils étaient une soixantaine à travailler: There were around sixty people working here at the height of the observatory, but there are only around fifteen at most today.
Nous la rejoignons après une journée de: We rejoin it after a day of slow sliding out of the glacial world, when the grass reappears in large islets and the relief seems to respond to the cry of the ptarmigan. Behind us, the glaciers descended the day before in the fog stretch their pale mass, giving the landscape a striking depth.
Le brouillard enveloppe des bâtiments hé: The fog envelops buildings inherited from the Soviet era, further accentuating their dilapidated character. A large man emerges from the mist and comes to meet us. He speaks to us in Russian and I respond with a sign illustrating the dodo. “Yann?” » “Da.” »
Il nous accompagne dans une contre-allée: He accompanies us down a side alley and we enter a period building, closed with double doors. The tiny entrance hall accommodates our skis, next to the kitchen area. A steep staircase with alternating steps leads us into a bright room, which in turn gives access to two blind rooms with, in each of them, an alcove bed. A table and 4 chairs complete the rudimentary equipment of the place.
Aux questionnements d’Amélie sur la prés: To Amélie's questions about the highly desired presence of a shower (I had sold them "comfortable" accommodation), he responded with a "niet." » It's so good to be in a heated room that this accommodation, by contrast, seems very comfortable to me. I enjoy the atmosphere of this place. I improvise a shower by hanging the water cow under the eaves of the entrance hall. Warm water on the stove softens the biting cold, while a few flakes linger in the calm air.
Scène de voyage et de ski de randonnée p: Travel scene and ski touring during the ski traverse of the Alatau Island massif, Kazakhstan, on day 4 of journeying.
Une visite des lieux s’impose. Je traver: A site visit is essential. I cross the main street and reach a large car park where a few cars are parked. I don't really know if I have the right to be there. I approach a man rummaging in his trunk. The pretext of the memory card allows me to approach it. He invites me to follow him. After climbing a wide staircase, we enter a large paneled room where a large billiard table sits. The floor, warped in places, has undoubtedly taken on water.
Nous poursuivons dans un long couloir, d: We continue down a long couloir, from which we escape through a bricked door to reach the upper floor. Up there, the same immense couloir stretches out again, leading to a small room furnished with a desk, a table and a sofa. After heating me a mug of instant coffee in the microwave, he takes out a phone with a cracked glass, extracts the memory card and hands it to me.
Je lui propose de venir déguster le rest: I suggest he come and taste the rest of Aurélien’s champagne as an aperitif. Igor is an active retiree. He has been a mechanical and electronic engineer on gamma telescopes since 1983 and maintains them, generally staying here for periods of 15 days.
Après le départ d’Igor, Amélie se retire: After Igor leaves, Amélie retreats and I sense something is happening. She needs to be alone, she tells me. At the meal, the atmosphere is heavy. I can see that this is not going well. So I start the discussion: “Are you upset about the trip? ". His last question to Igor was about how to get off from Tian-Shan station: 23 km on foot. This lack of alternative weighed on her, even if deep down, Amélie is a fighter who is not used to giving up. But she feels cornered with the unpleasant feeling of delaying us.
Elle a aussi besoin de se projeter sur l: She also needs to plan for the remaining steps. As a guide, we focus on the uncertainties linked to mountain conditions, perhaps sometimes obscuring human uncertainties, which are paradoxically easier to resolve, provided we provoke such moments of exchange. One thing is certain: this evening, everyone goes to bed with a lighter heart!
Le soleil se lève sur Tian-Shan, et sa p: The sun rises over Tian-Shan, and its dominant position expands the expanse of the mountains of Ile Alatau. A providential snow bridge allows us to cross the torrent to switch to the opposite slope. The horizon opens onto the Kazakh plain and its economic capital, Almaty, from where we left. The atmosphere is lighter today and the descent is delicious.
Au loin, nous apercevons notre petite ca: In the distance, we see our little cabin. It is a small sheet metal construction, with a gable roof and a small chimney. Aurélien jokes, wondering if we will be able to lie down. Surprisingly, it is rather modern in its construction: floor to ground, wall lining with wood-look plywood, double-glazed window. The bed bench is wedged under each foot but still far from being flat, and the door has disappeared, replaced by a wool blanket.
Assis dans nos duvets, nous lisons, écri: Sitting in our sleeping bags, we read, write, discuss, and sometimes we do nothing. It is not a question of waiting, since waiting means that there would be an end to reach, an outcome of something or an objective to fulfill. The almost imperceptible rustling of the snow which delicately settles on the tin roof of our small shelter adds an almost unreal sweetness to the silence.
Peut-être formulons-nous l’espoir, en ch: Perhaps we express the hope, in each of us, that this time stolen from our frenetic existences will never end or be disrupted by any obstacle. This is our last evening in the Kazakh mountains. It is joyful, because all these adventures have often made us doubt the outcome of the journey. But it is also tinged with nostalgia, these passages of life being ephemeral, a condition of their existence and the incarnation of a cherished rarity.
Scène de voyage et de ski de randonnée p: Travel scene and ski touring during the ski traverse of the Alatau Island massif, Kazakhstan, on day 5 of journeying.
Demain, nous achèverons notre traversée: Tomorrow, we will finish our crossing at a beautiful summit dominating the immense Kazakh plain, as far as the eye can see, from where we will be able to measure the distance covered. Then there will be the slow descent, literally and figuratively, which I know is long and uncertain. We will meet Kazakhs who are intrigued to see us arriving from mountains that are inaccessible to them in winter. They will offer us a bowl of soup as a mark of hospitality abroad. Then we will go and get drunk in the bars of Almaty to forget this brutal return to modern civilisation.
En tant que guide, j’ai atteint avec cet: As a guide, I have achieved with this journeying both the embodiment of what I want to experience as a professional and a limit of what I am ready to accept as an engagement with clients. This trip pushed me to my limits and the accident probably strongly colored this feeling. But in the end, what a journey!

Kosovo à ski : traversée des montagnes d: Kosovo on skis: crossing the Šar mountains

Entre Albanie, Macédoine du Nord et Koso: Between Albania, North Macedonia and Kosovo
La traversée des montagnes de Šar est né: Crossing the Šar mountains was born from an old desire: to go skiing in a country loaded, for me, with family and political history. I knew Kosovo through the story of my father, who was involved in humanitarian work at the end of the 1990s. I wrote this trip as I would have liked to tell it to him.
Neuf jours de ski au long cours, de vill: Nine days of long-distance skiing, from village to village, between Albania, Kosovo and Macedonia. Here, the question is not so much the summit as the possibility of moving forward each day, of finding a passage, a roof, a café. A crossing made of constant adjustments and encounters, where the line is drawn as much on the ground as in human relationships.

L'énonciation du nom d'un pays résonne s: Saying the name of a country often resonates with ideas, sometimes preconceived, or memories. Kosovo is the Kosovars, sometimes used in expressions that praise their pugnacity. But for me, Kosovo is above all a country where my father went on a humanitarian mission, at the turn of the 2000s, on behalf of MSF. When I returned from a trip to Georgia last April, I shared with him my wish to go skiing in this Balkan country. He remained silent on the subject, and I then understood that the Kosovo war and his trip there had marked him, for the atrocities he saw there. Since then, my father has left this earth, and behind the cruel frustration of not being able to tell him my story with Kosovo, I decided to write it.
Le Kosovo, dans l'expérience que j'en av: Kosovo, in the experience I had through my father, was therefore a war. A recent war, at the gates of Europe which took place in 1998-1999. A bloody war, with genocidal features, under the cover of ethnic tensions between Albanians and Serbs and territorial issues. At the time, Slobodan Milošević's Serbia wanted to regain control of Kosovo, which was an autonomous province of Serbia in the former Yugoslavia. The war therefore opposed the army of the Serbian regime and the Kosovo Liberation Army (UCK), soon supported by NATO forces, via KFOR. Kosovo then came under UN administration, before declaring its independence in 2008. An independence which is not unanimously recognised, including by certain EU countries.
Le Kosovo n'est a priori pas une destina: Kosovo is not a priori a ski destination. The idea of ​​going there was given to me by Jean Annequin, five years ago. At the end of confinement, he supervised training in organising trips and came back delighted with the adventure experienced there. Experiencing poor weather conditions, they were unable to ski exactly the planned line, namely the crossing from Radomirë, in Albania, to the eastern end of the range, between Kosovo and Macedonia. Taking inspiration from their route, I spent hours on the maps to find a line that crosses the entire massif on skis, with the desire to visit villages in the three border countries: Albania to the west, Macedonia from north to south and Kosovo to the north. I hesitated to know in which direction to carry out this raid, and it seemed more appropriate to aim for descents to the north and to carry out the big obligatory stages at the start. To leave Albania to reach Kosovo and Macedonia at the end of the third day. This crossing of the Sharr Mountains was a long journey. Nine days of skiing, from village to village, with significant elevation changes and sometimes long distances to cover.
The Albanian part, from Peshkopi to Brod.
Après deux bonnes heures de bus depuis T: After a good two hours on the bus from Tirana, the cold hit us when we got off the bus. Peshkopi is already very lively. As soon as we get off, several taxi drivers come to offer us their service, but our priority is more focused on coffee and a heated place. All you have to do is cross the street, as someone else would say, to find… a café. We enter a double room, almost empty. Only a group of elders are seated at a table, smoking. It seems to us from another time to smoke freely in these places. The coffees, very strong, just like the chocolates, “denso”, are like those we drink in Italy. A final section by taxi, and we arrive at the start of our crossing. Zimur, a mosque, three houses and an elder, who stands at a distance and stares at us suspiciously. Or maybe interrogative. We go up a ridge which overlooks vast plains, and the contrast of colours is striking. The mist rises up to us, and with it the emanations of smoke from the wood fires which, everywhere in the valleys here, heat the houses. It's strange to smell these smells so high up. The descent of Maja Grames (2344m), the first summit of the traverse, consists of a long traverse. It is past noon but the snow has not softened. This makes the operation much easier, saving us time and energy. After crossing a small pass, a second long crossing allows us to reach the heights of the village of Radomirë, a stopover for the next two nights. We barely begin to see the village and its imposing mosque when the muezzin begins to sing. What a change of scenery! We arrive at the Radomira hotel and enter a large bar room where a handcrafted stove takes pride of place. A cylinder where 4 feet are welded, a bottom and a lid, a hole for the evacuation of fumes through an elbow tube, which crosses half of the room and almost seems to go down. And yet, this stove fires damn well. It alone heats the entire room, despite the windows constantly being open to evacuate cigarette smoke.
Trois skieurs suivant la trace sur une c: Three skiers following the track on a ridge of the šar, western sector of the Šar massif, near the Korab, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Skieur solitaire avançant sur le fil enn: Lone skier advancing on the snowy line, western sector of the Šar massif, near the Korab, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Nous ne sommes pas seuls dans la montée: We are not alone in the climb to the highest point in Kosovo. A young Frenchman, in jeans and sneakers, decided to climb the Korab at all costs. Despite sharing our doubts, we will find him at the summit and, much later, at the hotel. For two days, Mount Korab plays on us, because we cannot really identify its summit precisely among the peaks that surround us. From the summit an immense, relatively flat expanse unfolds. The very one we will have to cross the next day, the key day of this crossing. We opt for a descent on the other side, allowing us to leave the skis at the snow line to facilitate the start of the next day's stage. Back in the village, we come across two elders, who offer us a cigarette, as an invitation to chat. Everyone refuses, and out of politeness or to accept the invitation, I take one from the package, which I will rub. The exchange is above all gestural. This evening we take time to chat with our host, Billy. At age 15, his family sent him to live in England, where he worked as a carpenter for 8 years. He returned last year to work in the family hotel, which he is partly renovating to enlarge the existing rooms. Now he works here, in this bar room where the men meet, smoking and playing cards.
Groupe de skieurs réuni sur une crête pa: Group of skiers gathered on a panoramic ridge, upper Brod valley, Šar massif, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Skieur déclenchant un virage dans une pe: Skier initiating a turn on a powdery slope, upper Brod valley, Šar massif, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
C'est le jour J. La grosse étape du raid: It's the big day. The big stage of the raid, not only for the 2000m of altitude difference, but above all for the distance to cover, almost 40km. At 5 a.m., when we arrive in the bar room, Billy and his father are already busy. Two empty coffee cups reflect a moment of sharing before starting the work day. The kitchen door is ajar, and we see a woman busy behind the scenes for a moment, before the father closes the door... The first pass is a good overview, as is the endless pseudo-descending traverse, where the objective is to achieve as much elevation as possible. At the bottom of the descent, an old algeco marking the border between Kosovo and Macedonia marks for us the start of the longest climb of the day: around ten kilometres, almost flat. The last climb takes place in the evening lights. At the summit, we see Mount Korab in the distance, and this vast plateau which separates us and which we crossed after many hours. This small massif displays all its immensity here. It's grandiose. We quickly reach the top of the Arxhena station. The slopes are concrete, and obviously the snow groomer will not pass this evening... Brod is our first Kosovar stop. When we enter the “restaurant”, a bar serving small meals, around twenty looks point towards us, probably these looks are not threatening, but they are heavy and I do not dare, unconsciously, to cross them, preferring to flee towards the room on the first floor where the owner takes us. We order “Peja” and seven “burgers”. The plates that we are served consist of a minced steak stuffed with cheese, a sort of upside-down burger, all garnished with a few slices of vegetables. Next comes a plate of toast. We celebrate this first day with a bottle of champagne from Aurélien Lurquin, the group's winemaker. A 2020 Chardonnay, from Les Traverses parcel, which puts us at ease, while subtly awakening our taste buds. Probably more than the single dish of the evening, which nevertheless has the merit of filling our bellies…
Skieurs progressant dans l’immensité bla: Skiers progressing in the white immensity, western sector of the Šar massif, near the Korab, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Grands plateaux enneigés sous une lumièr: Large snow-covered plateaus under golden light, upper Brod valley, Šar massif, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Brod - Lubinje e Posthme : à saute-mouto: Brod - Lubinje e Posthme: leapfrog on the border between Macedonia and Kosovo
Ce matin, la pleine lune m'a tiré du lit: This morning the full moon got me out of bed early. I was already in front of the mosque when the intoxicating song of the muezzin was spit out through saturated loudspeakers. Looking for an open café, with the pretext of visiting the village. This morning, a mission awaits me, quickly transformed into a trap, which I define as dispossession of control of one's time by a local. The beginning is therefore the wait in our host's store, Brod's “mini-pizza market”, then the arrival of an old VW combi, which he calls out to. It's the taxi, he told me. We take a seat, and, after 200m, the driver stops in a street offering us a “coffee”, the only universal word that we understand, whatever the language. We go upstairs to a place that we would never have designated as such, and the owner immediately offers us a “macchiato”. Here too, the Italian influence is obviously important. The taxi driver, Bilgaip, lights his cigarette with his coffee. Then another. Then another. And time flies, I wonder if he is still aware that we have agreed on a return trip to Dragash. So I decide to keep a few gaps in this time over which I have lost control, and I head towards the “Burek” sign where a man is busy making a kind of cheese puff pastry, twirling it in the air to stretch it, with impressive dexterity. When I come back to the café after meeting the whole group, it's probably time to leave. During the journey, around ten kilometres, three cigarettes were smoked by our driver, window closed and only open to remove the cigarette butts. Dragash is a town without a soul, but with the hustle and bustle of the city and its amenities, including a supermarket and an ATM. These are euros that I am withdrawing, although Kosovo is neither a member of the EU, nor therefore of the euro zone. After the war, the Yugoslav dinar was replaced for a time by the German mark, then by the euro in 2002, which became the main currency without an official agreement with the ECB. Kosovo therefore uses the euro unilaterally, without being able to issue it. Then begins a long wait. I no longer control anything. Bilgaip tells me that he is waiting for two people, but I cannot tell if they are really people he is waiting for, or if it is to fill his taxi. He waits in the street, wandering from one store to another, without showing that he is a taxi driver and that he is going to Brod. When the wait becomes heavy, we decide to resume our time and push open the door of the café opposite. The atmosphere is suffocating there, with so many people smoking in this enclosed space without ventilation. We order 3 coffees, telling the waiter that we will drink them on the terrace. By the time the coffees are served to us, it seems that our driver is finally ready to leave. Quickly swallowed, we get back into the old combi, which stops a few hundred metres further on, for I don't know what reason. Bilgaip leaves and enters a shop, returning laden with a crate of bottles. We hit the road again, and another stop. This one will last until I explicitly state that we really need to go back to Brod. It's already 10 a.m., and a long day of skiing awaits us.
Nous partons à pied dans une vallée enca: We set off on foot in a deep valley, where the path quickly dies into numerous intermittent herd paths, using both sides. We play leapfrog above the river, playing with the frozen shells of the stones emerging from the watercourse. In the distance, the valley turns, and I hope to find continuous snow behind it. From Kleç (2414m), we descend a few hundred metres on the Macedonia side, before climbing to Zallinë (2494m) by a slope indicated at less than 30° on my map, but which, in reality, is much steeper. It remains to optimize the snow for the descent. I am aiming for a path much further east, and the descent consists, as often since the beginning of this journey, of crossing on the side. I am happy with my journey, from tongues of snow to tongues of snow, which becomes quite an exhilarating game, until they become too scattered. We can't stop Pascal, who heads straight down the slope in ski boots. We soon take out the headlamps, and move through fields of dried ferns covered by snow, weaving between the scrub bushes. Soon, we join a cattle trail not marked on the map, which takes us to the village. The apartment we enter is freezing, as is the shower. I need some time to decompress, an aperitif to appreciate the day we have just had. This bucolic climb along the river, these lights of the sunset, which here seem to last an eternity, the arrival above the village of Bozovce, which appeared surreptitiously around a bend. I need to enjoy, without doing anything, just sipping my coke. No beer this evening, to the misfortune of Aurélien, the group's winemaker who doesn't seem accustomed to this. The meal is light compared to the efforts made during the day, and it is with our bellies not completely stretched that we go to bed, lacking starch or a good dose of protein! Mattresses on the floor, a convertible sofa with basic comfort and a small radiant heater which has difficulty heating the room adequately. This first evening in Macedonia is more rustic than the previous nights…

File de skieurs sur une vaste étendue bl: Line of skiers on a vast white expanse, upper Brod valley, Šar massif, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Ce matin, nous sommes réveillés par l'ap: This morning, we were awakened by the call of the muezzin at 5:53 a.m. I remove my earplugs to better appreciate this song which reminds me of this trip to Africa with my father, to drive down a Peugeot 504 in Mauritania, when I was around ten years old. The village of Bozovce seems poorer than Brod, where we were the day before. Although the main streets are paved, many paths are still dirt, and many houses are in ruins or abandoned. Here, the stone walls of the houses are built with regularly placed horizontal wooden bays.
Lorsque nous pénétrons dans la pénombre: When we enter the darkness of the room, the cigarette smoke is suffocating. We are in the only café in Bozovce, where around ten men spread across several tables are drinking coffee and smoking cigarettes. The tables are arranged on the sides, and we have the impression of entering the middle of an assembly, where time seems to stand still. It stretches and fills the inactivity of everyday life. Our presence here, in the middle of winter, is unusual, we feel it. One of them speaks Italian well, and I strike up a conversation. He worked for 11 years as a mason in Italy before returning here, to the village, to do odd jobs. But he spends most of his time here, in the café. I offer him one, and as it's tricky not to offer one to others, I offer coffee to everyone. The bartender, who seems to know the habits of each of his customers, serves anyone who wants a sweet espresso or a latte. For us, they open the door to the café, letting out the fumes of cigarette smoke, as well as the heat from the stove in the middle of the room. But as soon as we leave, the door closes behind us. And behind closed doors, these men continue to smoke, to appreciate the passing of time. Here we go again on foot, on a path which is not indicated on the map but which I found by examining the aerial images. This morning, despite the southern slope, the snow is not far away, and continuous snow cover is reached in around twenty minutes. We go up a plateau, cross old skier tracks, then a slope which should be below 30° on the map, but which is in reality much steeper. I am happy that the snow cover is also frozen, because it would not be the same adventure if the snow conditions turned out to be unstable... Arriving at the ridge, we follow it on its southern slope, until reaching the summit of Vërtop (2555m). For the first time since the start of the raid, the slope that I had initially planned leaves me doubtful. I am committed all the same, to appreciate the composition of the snow cover: there is a patch of around thirty centimeters, rather compact, and below a much looser layer. The wide slope and this configuration make me give up for another less steep slope, from the pass. The snow isn't so bad. Packed powder, sometimes blown and irregular. But given the quality of the snow we've been skiing since the beginning, we're happy with it! By a large crossing, we reach the initial slope. The magnitude of this slope and its steepness give me shivers, but I bless this very stable snow conditions. The first couloir I overlook is ravaged by an old avalanche of wet snow. The second, which I had planned to descend, is smooth in its first part, but quickly becomes unskiable. We have to take a tangent, into a very dense beech forest, where Aurélien tries and fails in a balancing act that only he has the gift for, ending up perched in a tree.
Lubinje e Poshtme est étonnante. Il n'y: Lubinje e Poshtme is amazing. There are almost only new houses or houses under construction. But our accommodation is far from the town and we have to climb a good hundred metres in altitude. It is an isolated house in the mountains, and the owner welcomes us warmly, calling to me when we arrive: “Yann”. They are an old couple, whose son is exiled in Geneva. They run a fish restaurant here, linked to a km0 trout farm. We are hungry, and the way we all sit at the table expresses it explicitly. It's only 17:00, but we start eating a meal, without knowing whether it's a late lunch or an early dinner. After raw vegetable dishes, 7 grilled trout arrive. So much so that the skin on our stomachs is very tight when we leave the table, but it's only 18:00, and at 20:00, we're already back at the same point: almost hungry! But our hosts have gone back down to the village, and we only have a case of beer to sustain us…
Skieur progressant sur une arête balayée: Skier progressing on a windswept ridge, Dragash and Brod sector, Šar massif, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.

Notre hôte est au petit soin, s'enquéran: Our host takes great care, often asking about the quality of the breakfast he offers us: the marinated peppers and homemade jam are real gems. His beautiful blue eyes and his friendly gaze make him endearing. He takes out a rather approximate map of the Sharr mountains to help us understand our route for the day, writing to me using a translation application that it seems “arduous” to him.
Nous partons, comme à l'accoutumée, à pi: We set off, as usual, on foot and loaded with skis, into a magnificent beech forest. We put on shoes as usual around 1400m, then we reach the border ridge, gradually covered in fog. Change of plan: there is no point in following the edge with your head on the handlebars with this visibility, so we take the tangent, to reach the pass rather than the summit. Aside from the poor visibility, the snow is no worse, almost good compared to previous days. On sight and on the map, I'm not doing too badly, especially by opting for the right couloir. It's exhilarating to make bets like this, and to see that they turn out to be good. For the first time since the start of the stay, we arrived at the hotel on skis. The Prevallë pass is an atypical place. It's not a ski resort, but it has all the hallmarks of one, consisting mainly of hotels, restaurants and villas for rent. We are far from the small village of Bozovce which we left this morning. On the other hand, the Krojet hotel in which we are sleeping this evening is clearly above the rest in terms of standard compared to the accommodation visited so far. A large reception room is heated by two wood stoves, one of which is surrounded by armchairs that inspire relaxation. Wood reigns supreme, enhancing the warm side. Several waiters are busy at the bar, strangely differentiating between “cappuccinos” and “macchiatos”. The two cups are equal, but on the milk foam of the first a flower is drawn with a chocolate cream that is too sweet. While the macchiato resembles a well-made Italian cappuccino, with the flower drawn in the milk foam. In addition to this Kosovar subtlety, the dishes here are mainly composed of meat, and desserts do not exist. Hot chocolates, thick as in Italy, proved to be the best compromise to end the meal with a sweet touch.
Compagnons et hôtes réunis autour de la: Companions and guests gathered around the table, western sector of the Šar Mountains National Park, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Skieur progressant dans la neige avec de: Skier progressing through the snow with two dogs, western sector of the Šar Mountains National Park, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Je n'ai pas réussi à négocier un petit d: I didn't manage to negotiate breakfast before 8 a.m., but on the other hand, at 8 a.m. sharp, the table was filled with several platters of dishes, such as marinated peppers, kiri, eggs poached in oil, or some other form of cheese spread, all accompanied by oily fritters. This morning, around ten dogs are with us and four of them, more daring, will accompany us all day. The sky gets darker as we climb, so much so that we find ourselves in the clouds again at the summit of Bister (2651m). The small layer of snow that fell between yesterday and tonight is irregular due to the wind, and requires careful skiing. But the further down we go, the more homogeneous and pleasant the thin layer of powder becomes to ski, so much so that we end up skiing the best snow of the stay, our cursor having descended very low. We enter a sparse pine forest, which marks a sudden change in vegetation. These forests seem more skiable than the beech forests, which are sometimes very dense. It also changes the atmosphere of skiing, because although the beech trees are very tall, the pines are almost at eye level, opening up the landscape. After a long crossing on the side, we go up a steep shoulder which allows us to reach the Brezovicë station.
Brezovicë est une station de ski d'un au: Brezovicë is a ski resort from another time. The first ski lifts were installed at the dawn of the 1980s, and it was then identified as an alternative site for the ski events of the Sarajevo 1984 Winter Olympic Games. Since the Kosovo War in 1998-1999, it received no investment for its maintenance or modernization, until the providential arrival of the French group "Compagnie des Alpes" in 2014, which had planned to invest more than 400 million euros. This modernization plan ultimately did not see the light of day, and the station remained as it was. We arrive at the car park, and an impressive pile of rubbish. An open-air dump that doesn't say its name. This sets the tone for our experience at this resort. We walk back towards the ski lifts and our hotel. An old building, whose management was taken over the previous winter. Aside from a poorly done lick of white paint and a change of furniture, the building must not have received a major renovation in decades. Just like the huge hotel above us, built on the snow front, in a layout very similar to our third generation Alpine resorts. The hall which serves as reception is huge and houses a small market, where you can mainly find sweet products. Downstairs, in the bar room, the owners smoke cigarettes and drink coffee. The smell of tobacco is disgusting.
Deux skieurs et un chien suivant la trac: Two skiers and a dog following the trail, Prevalla sector, Šar Mountains National Park, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Skieurs réunis au-dessus des vallées du: Skiers gathered above the šar valleys, Prevalla sector, Šar Mountains National Park, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Nous sommes heureux de quitter cette sta: We are happy to leave the ski resort, though glad to have had the experience. We climb the eastern side of a ridge among the pines, all the way to the summit above. Mist rises on the Macedonian side, and we take advantage of a gap for a fine descent on spring snow. The further we go, the better the snow gets. The second ascent is entirely in fog and takes us to Kyne (2324m). Then comes an incredible descent down a long couloir on the Macedonian side, playing with the mist and the spring snow. The welcome at Ljuboten hut, built in 1931 and Macedonia’s oldest mountain hut, is warm. The two wardens, enormous men with teddy-bear eyes, are volunteers for the Tetovo Alpine Club. We enter a low-ceilinged room heated by a wood-burning stove. Beers are ordered immediately and arrive as pints. We know the adventure is drawing to a close, and there is a general easing of tension tonight, a good-natured atmosphere: we know we have just lived through quite an odyssey. The meal is gargantuan from starter to dessert, to Étienne’s delight and our misfortune. John Deer will be rumbling all night…
Deux skieurs traversant un versant domin: Two skiers crossing a slope overlooking the plain, Brezovica sector, Šar Mountains, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Voyageur devant une maison de pierre et: Traveller in front of a stone and wood house, eastern sector of the Šar Mountains, towards Ljuboten, during a ski traverse of Kosovo.
Pour ce neuvième et dernier jour de trav: For this ninth and last day of crossing, the programme is finally lighter, with a little less than 1000m of elevation gain to reach the last summit to the east of the massif, the Maja e Lubotenit. After tacking around to find continuous snow cover, the gamble of aiming for the SE valley proved to be the right one. We leave it to take a foothold on a beautiful ridge, comfortable on skis. Between the layers of clouds and the play of the mist, we can intermittently appreciate part of the path already covered. The mountain, today, only appears in fragments, unfolding the immensity of the landscape by a line of flight which tends towards infinity, the horizon being nebulous, beyond the sea of ​​clouds which we dominate. Summit, we savor the moment. For a final descent, we couldn't have dreamed of anything better. Slope, square and spring snow, just right. We can finally ski without fearing sudden snow changes. I can't help but let go, and sometimes reach the limits of my equipment, the lightness of the skis and boots, favored for the climb, not really being compatible with the speed and the micro-reliefs... We soon find ourselves under the layer, and smell, as on the first day, the smoke emanations from the homes in the valley. It becomes less obvious to anticipate the route to optimize intermittent snow. The fog is so dense that we end up getting soaked by the drizzle. Scratching and ending up skiing frost in a ditch, and a few lost stones here and there, we take off our shoes 50m from the road. Sometimes, things are done well, since the road crossed, we push the door of an open restaurant. There is no one in the room, and the waiters don't seem unhappy to see us arrive. The restaurant room honors the wood, and makes you want to sit down and share a good meal. We couldn't have asked for better and I immediately ordered a burst of pizza. At 3 euros for a Margherita and 6.5 euros for the most expensive pizza, you could expect to be served either small or mediocre pizzas. Our prejudices will be destroyed.
Pristina. Je pensais débarquer dans un g: Pristina. I was thinking of arriving at a large establishment, but the hotel I booked is a small family run hotel. The son welcomes us, intrigued to see us disembark with skis. His family is of Albanian origin. His two grandfathers and his uncle were killed by the Serbs during the war 25 years ago. After dinner, we set off in search of a place to spend the evening, and perhaps part of the night. Pristina is much nicer than what we saw from Tirana. The pedestrian street, wide and paved with stone, is decorated with Albanian and Kosovar flags. Soon we enter a bar called “Bubble”. No bouncer at the entrance, no filtering and for good reason, we realise that the relaxed atmosphere comes from its attendance. There are many men, few women, and they are rather effeminate in their clothing or their attitude. A Drag queen arrives and sets the dance floor on fire. We are in a queer bar, in a country where more than 90% of the population is Muslim. It just goes to show that prejudices are right…

Nous sommes bringuebalés dans une vieill: We are rattling around in an old Peugeot 405. Four hundred and twenty thousand kilometres on the clock. At each elevation of the terrain, the underbody scrapes the dirt track, wet from the rain which has been pouring down since the middle of the night. Above us, vast sections of mountains and an embankment destabilized by the earthworks of the road. Mohammed sings, his gloved hands grip the steering wheel. Mohammed prays.
Derrière moi, Julien est pâle. Depuis sa: Behind me, Julien is pale. From his half-open foggy window, he watches the falling stones, in a heavy silence. His jacket protects him from the gusts of wind which push the rain inside the passenger compartment.
Nous redescendons de Tizgui, un petit vi: We come back down from Tizgui, a small Berber village lost to the west of the Toubkal national park. Last stage of a journey where the term adventure took on its full meaning. The adventure, like a game with uncertainties: those of the mountains, of which we are accustomed, and those, more local, of the Moroccan administration... and, suffice to say, the latter disconcerted us.

D’entrée de jeu, la neige s’est immiscée: From the outset, the snow interfered with the plans, making them unrealistic and requiring them to be urgently recomposed. This snow, which nevertheless called us here, pushes me to my limits. Forty centimeters in the streets of Imlil. Rare event. We are lucky.
Depuis hier soir, j’ai changé de *mindse: Since yesterday evening, I’ve changed my *mindset*. The original plan has become completely obsolete, and the time for planning anything is over. I just want to open up the possibilities, to be able to improvise.
Hier, nous sommes venus d’Imlil à ski, a: Yesterday, we came from Imlil on skis, after landing the same morning in Marrakech. The mountain roads beyond were cut off by snow. In a hurry, we prepared our bags for six days of skiing, leaving all the excess with Hassan, our driver, who will bring them back to us on the last day.
Imlil. Nous chaussons les skis au cœur d: Imlil. We put on skis in the heart of the city. Residents are busy clearing snow from flat roofs, because water seeps into them when the snow melts. On every corner of the alley, Berbers offer us tea, intrigued by our paraphernalia. There, a small snowy ramp is the place for various slides for the village kids: some on sleds, others on trash bags, others still on skis, sometimes wearing sneakers.

Nous rejoignons le Tizi n’Tamatert, d’où: We reach Tizi n’Tamatert, from where the north faces of Likemt and Igounouane appear, imposing and laden with snow. Passing the pass marks a clear change in atmosphere: the fresh wind and powder of the Tacchdirt slope replace the stifling heat and soggy snow of the Imlil slope.
Tacchdirt s’illumine doucement, tandis q: Tacchdirt lights up gently, while the muezzin sings. We reach the village at dusk. Ibrahim welcomes us with all the gratitude I know, forged during our numerous telephone exchanges.
Indécision. L’option Likemt, point de dé: Indecision. The Likemt option, starting point for a possible crossing of the Toubkal on skis, comes to mind, but it is very risky. There are too many uncertainties about snowpack conditions. Our tired minds have little energy left to make a good decision, which is in fact postponed until tomorrow.
Au petit matin, la force du collectif ai: In the early morning, with the strength of the collective helping us, we decide to explore the Ourika valley, east of the Oukaimeden station. The day before, we had spotted skiers going down the Tizi n'Ou Addi, and a long horizontal trace which allowed us to reach the valley from Tacchdirt.
Nous traversons les pentes sud en suivan: We cross the southern slopes following these footprints. They reach the hanging village of Talate n’Chaoute, and its mosque with its pink minaret, like everywhere here.
Au sommet de la combe, le Tizi n’Ou Addi: At the top of the valley, the Tizi n’Ou Addi gives access to a beautiful powder slope little affected by the wind. The initial plan was to go eat a tagine in Oukaimeden, but the slight slope of the valley quickly discouraged us.
Juste au-dessus du Tizi n’Itbir, le col: Just above the Tizi n’Itbir, the pass which connects the Oukaimeden plateau and the Ourika valley, we are tempted to reach the small summit to the north. The wind has stopped and, as far as the eye can see, an arid expanse stretches. What a contrast!

La combe, longue et régulière, est délic: The valley, long and regular, is delicious to ski. Soon, we arrive at the first village, Agouns, from where we hear a surprising commotion, improbable in our eyes in such a remote place. Everywhere, the inhabitants are busy with their activities: the women are in the bed of the river, probably doing the laundry, some are tending the herds of cattle, the kids are playing.
Agouns est un village agro-pastoral perc: Agouns is an agro-pastoral village perched at around 2400 m altitude, the last douar in the upper Ourika valley. Organised in six small neighborhoods above terraces cultivated with barley, corn and some food vegetables (turnips, beans, potatoes), punctuated by rare walnut trees, it is only accessible in summer by a 4×4 track. In winter, you have to take the path on the mountainside to go down to Timichchi, where the asphalt road allows you to reach Sti Fadma, the town, more than ten kilometres downstream.
Cretes et descente en neige dans le mass: Ridges and snow descent in the Toubkal massif, Moroccan High Atlas
Nous pénétrons dans une belle demeure ma: We enter a beautiful masonry residence. With the traditional welcome tea, Brahim takes the time to tell us about the life of his village. Timichchi, 42 inhabitants, was bereaved by the earthquake of 2023. There were seven victims and many houses destroyed; some were rebuilt on the opposite bank of the river with government help.
Ce sont des maisons maçonnées, roses, qu: These are masonry, pink houses, which contrast with the historic stone constructions. The tagine is served with the muezzin singing. Brahim is getting ready to go and pray, like five times a day. Most of the time, he goes down to the mosque, which was once the social place on cold winter days. Everyone brought their own wood, and a large fire in the middle of the room livened up the conversations. This sociability has disappeared, Brahim points to the joint arrival of electricity and the internet.

Le lendemain, nous rejoignons Labassen a: The next day, we reach Labassen with the first rays of the sun.
Labassen est un village d’une vingtaine: Labassen is a village of around twenty houses, located in a small valley adjacent to the Ourika valley. A mountain village, without road access, cut off from the world as soon as the snow falls. The flat roofs of the houses become terraces occupied by the inhabitants, who settle there to enjoy the sun. Here, the houses are not heated.
Depuis l’ouverture d’une terrasse couver: Since the opening of a covered terrace, children have had fun greeting us. Women are there too, perhaps intrigued by our presence. Skiers must be rare here.
Nous rejoignons un vaste vallon aux cade: We reach a vast valley with thousand-year-old junipers. The faces above us are steep, striped by numerous ice waterfalls. Yesterday, looking at the map, it seemed possible to reach the summit of Bou Iguenouane by following the emerging ridge of Tizi Tacherddirt. Against all expectations, we reached the ridge quite easily, then, via an incursion on the south slope, the summit, in the wind and fog. Too bad, I really wanted to see Ouarzazate, and the desert. Where, when I was seven or eight years old, my father took me in 504 across the Sahara.
Tacchdirt. Lors du conciliabule du soir,: Tacchdirt. During the evening meeting, we decide to attempt crossing the massif towards its southern slope, being well aware that we will most likely have to exit via the south and the town of Amsouzart, because there is little chance that the weather on Saturday will leave us with the possibility of returning to Imlil on skis. Yallah!

Quand la police touristique s’en mêle: When the tourist police get involved
Ce soir-là, il y a du monde au gîte et,: That evening, there were people at the lodge and, in retrospect, everyone seemed to play a very particular role. First the snowblowers, finally arriving in Tacchdirt to open up the village. Then three Flemish Belgians, who came to ride, guided by Ibrahim’s brother. Two retired Pyrenees, opportunists like us, ski without a guide from the lodge.
Et Mohammed, frère d’Ibrahim, guide loca: And Mohammed, brother of Ibrahim, local guide, wearing a little purple cap, with a crooked smile. Friendly, but somewhat suspicious: he threatens to call the police because our planned crossing would violate the rules. But joking, we think. From this ludicrous scene, I understand that the host is responsible for the tourists he welcomes, and that our bivouac project at the Azib Likemt does not please him. Our discussions stop there. We are determined to maintain our project, the weather and snow conditions being favourable.

Refuge montagne ski randonnee dans le ma: Mountain ski and hiking hut in the Toubkal massif, Moroccan High Atlas
Nous quittons Ibrahim et son gîte pour r: We leave Ibrahim and his lodge to reach the road, perfectly cleared of snow. A young man in a traditional scarf leans against his scooter. I'm about to take out my camera, then I change my mind. He walks towards us and asks us… for our passports.
Mohammed était donc sérieux. Il nous a s: Mohammed was therefore serious. He undoubtedly left us ready, having left the lodge shortly before us, accompanying the two other French people, without a guide. That morning, our relationship with Ibrahim was strange. Something had changed compared to the closeness we had known to him until then. He didn't come to greet us when we left, even though we weren't supposed to see each other again. This surprised me. Perhaps he knew full well that it wasn't really a departure.
« Vous avez l’interdiction formelle d’al: “You are strictly prohibited from going to the mountains… without a local guide. » This is the refrain uttered to me on the phone by the tourist security manager. There is no possibility of discussion; “informal” arrangements are no longer appropriate. The game is lost.
Skieur porte refuge dans le massif du To: Skier takes hut in the Toubkal massif, Moroccan High Atlas
Je suis partagé sur cet événement, dont: I am divided on this event, which we are not accustomed to in our mountains. It took us by surprise, sending us the echo of arbitrary decisions, taken in a strong emotional context. Here the very recent deadly avalanche and the traumatic memory of the sordid assassination of two Scandinavian tourists at Azib Likemt in 2018. Indeed, we arrived in the Atlas the day after a tragedy linked to heavy snowfall: three Moroccan hikers, including a local guide, were swept away in an avalanche. The Moroccan administration, and particularly the “tourist police”, is tense: the “disappeared from Toubkal” have made the rounds in the Western media.
J’ai écrit à Mohammed ensuite, l’auxilia: I then wrote to Mohammed, the tourist police assistant, to ask him for the laws that govern our skiing in the Atlas Mountains, but I received no response.
De cet épisode, nous comprenons aussi qu: From this episode, we also understand that the local guide takes on an additional “social” role, that of protecting tourists in the face of potential reactions from locals. However, everywhere else, the welcome we received was very warm, including in the most remote and less touristy villages. And these are perhaps the most precious memories we will keep from this adventure.
Le Tazaghart (3 980 m), ou la fuite vers: Tazaghart (3,980 m), or escape to the wild mountain
À la lueur des phares de sa Dacia, Hassa: In the light of the headlights of his Dacia, Hassan drives up the road to the small village of Tizi Oussem. He makes us feel that he doesn't like this road. After the pharaonic construction of a hydroelectric dam, the wide, asphalted road was transformed into an earthen track, with unstable lower sides.
Nous avons été expulsés des montagnes de: We had been expelled from the mountains of Tacchdirt: *persona non grata*, tourists whose media profile would be too high if anything happened to us. We needed to find somewhere less controlled, less closely watched. We had arrived in the Atlas the day after a tragedy: three Moroccan hikers, including a local guide, had been swept away in an avalanche. The Moroccan authorities, particularly the ‘tourist police’, were on edge: coverage of the ‘missing hikers of Toubkal’ had spread through the Western media.
Sans l’importante chute de neige la veil: Without the heavy snowfall the day before our arrival, Tizi Oussem should have been the starting point for our crossing of Toubkal.
Montee vers les hautes pentes dans le ma: Climb to the high slopes in the Toubkal massif, Moroccan High Atlas
Quelques coups de fil de notre chauffeur: A few phone calls from our driver to friends of friends dropped us off at the entrance to a gîte, in the dark. The paint is peeling off the ceilings and scattering the mattresses like confetti. We are invited to follow our guests into the hammam. The young man measures the hot and cold water into a large bucket, and a smaller bucket is used to sprinkle himself. The ground is hot, and the smell of fuel oil tells us how it is heated. When the older of the two Berbers begins to vigorously rub my upper body, I understand that showering here is a collective rite...
Au programme, la Tazaghart, 2 200 m plus: On the programme, the Tazaghart, 2,200 m higher. Here, there are no obstacles, a priori. Insha’Allah.
Le chemin remonte d’abord un flanc de mo: The path first goes up a mountainside amid imposing juniper trees, before arriving at Azib Tamsoult and its namesake hut. Then, two bottlenecks appear in purple on my slope maps, and constitute uncertain passages. The first is exposed, but passable on skis. The second leaves me doubtful: an ice waterfall blocks the passage. I'm hesitant because there may be other alternatives. The wind has picked up and it is already late: I know that this decision will not count on a second chance. It seems that the right edge of the waterfall is thin, passable with the help of the rock. Bingo!
Depuis le Tizi Malooan, il ne semblait p: From Tizi Malooan, there did not seem to be any difficulty on my map, but a rocky ledge blocks our access to the summit. A small hidden couloir is hidden behind a tower. Without certainty, I commit to it. Once again, a rocky ledge blocks our access. I cross it not without difficulty, and I help my companions with the help of my stick. We soon stand at the summit, jostled by violent gusts and caught in thick fog.
