Monteur ski couloir neige dans le massif: Snow couloir ski fitter in the Toubkal massif, Moroccan High Atlas
Je suis coutumier du vent et du brouilla: I am used to wind and fog, but less familiar with this Moroccan frost, freezing rain which lacerates our faces and covers us with a thin sheet of opaque ice. The summit gives access to the vast Tazaghart plateau, swept by the winds and partly bare. Cockscombs are real traps, like fog, confusing us without us being aware of it.
Coup d’œil à mon téléphone : je me suis: Check my phone: I got pulled too far to the left, to the west end of the plateau. We have to go up against the squalls to find the right direction, to accept that we can no longer see anything, to delegate control of our skis to kinesthetics.
Derniers virages dans l’Atlas, fin du sk: Last turns in the Atlas, end of skiing, but not of the adventure.
Tizgui est un petit village de montagne: Tizgui is a small, lively mountain village. The main artery is a muddy track that is particularly busy at the end of the day. The muezzin begins to sing: without looking at the time, we know that it is 19:00 Another good day! Our ice sheets have melted, we are now soaked by the rain which continues to fall.
D’aspect extérieur, le gîte semble récen: From the outside, the cottage appears recent. Hussein, our host, must be 70 years old. His look is mischievous and friendly. The language barrier is frustrating: here, no one speaks French. We fill out the traditional register and our passports are photographed, like every evening. The last visitors recorded in this register were in March 2025! Here, tourist pressure is much less than around Imlil.
Toutes nos affaires sont trempées, et no: All our belongings are soaked, and we ask if it is possible to have additional heating. While we are enjoying a little “Marquise” (editor’s note: local cigarette) on the roof terrace with Julien, we suddenly smell the pleasant smell of the wood fire. The smell is coming from the stairwell. Strange, there was no fireplace in the lodge. We look at each other, sharing the same question: “Where could they have lit a fire?!”.
Le petit poêle portable trône au milieu: The small portable stove sits in the middle of the living room, the fire crackles. Hussein and his grandson, Mohammed, sit around the fireplace, enjoying the warmth. The fumes begin to invade the space, and the means of their evacuation remain enigmatic... The intention was generous and laudable, but our belongings remain too soaked to dry like this. The tagine is delicious, it is undoubtedly the best since our arrival.
Après les mandarines et la tisane, alors: After the tangerines and herbal tea, as we get ready to go to sleep, Hussein brings us a dish of couscous. Happy incomprehension. We have no choice but to honor him! Hussein stays there, we exchange looks. He shares tea with us. And this non-verbal presence is, for us, the sign of a warm welcome.

During this trip I learned a lot. This is the first time that everything does not go as planned, that the line deviates, that its path imagined upstream does not come true. If we are always ready to deal with the uncertainties of the mountain, those of the administration, when they are felt to be arbitrary, are always more difficult to accept. Morocco has its rules, and we have to deal with them.
J’avais entendu parler de l’obligation d: I had heard about the obligation to take a local guide, but according to contradictory statements. I didn’t know that bivouac was “forbidden”. But is it really? What is perhaps more disturbing is the lack of control by local authorities resulting from being “in the wild”, both literally and figuratively.
De cette tentative de traversée, j’ai dé: From this crossing attempt, I have already built my ideal line for the next trip to the Atlas. A line that stops in villages that are not very touristy, because these moments of meeting are among the most memorable experiences of this Moroccan journey. A line that leaves from the southwest of the massif, where there is no tourist pressure, and which deliberately avoids the Toubkal and its hustle and bustle! We can’t wait for it to snow again there so we can return with skis to this contrasting massif.

Skier au milieu des cades centenaires: Skiing in the middle of century-old junipers
Nous sommes bringuebalés dans une vieill: We are rattling around in an old Peugeot 405. Four hundred and twenty thousand kilometres on the clock. At each hill, the underbody scrapes the track soaked by the rain that fell all night. Above us, vast sections of mountains and an unstable slope. Mohammed sings, his gloved hands grip the steering wheel. Mohammed prays.
Skier ici n'a rien d'évident. La neige e: Skiing here is not easy. Snow is rare, but when it does start to fall, it can be capricious, requiring constant recomposition of the route. The High Atlas offers us arid valleys, high plateaus swept by gusts of wind and remote valleys where century-old junipers grow.

La der des ders ! Et encore une fois, il: The last of the last! And once again, we had to compose. We were initially supposed to do the classic Bernina tour, but the huge collapse that occurred on 14 April in Val Roseg, the problem of which I had finally managed to resolve, then the bad weather forecast once again directed me towards Austria.
De l'Ötztal, je ne connaissais qu'Ötzi,: From the Ötztal, I only knew Ötzi, this perfectly preserved mummy, found by chance in 1991, and dating from 3 millennia BC. The immense glaciers, clearly visible on the aerial maps and the large network of huts attracted me to organise these 5 days of journeying straddling the weekend of 1 May.
Après avoir placé tous les refuges sur l: After placing all the shelters on the map and ensuring that they have an open winter room, I still had to find the right combination. And between the initial project and the composition of the journey in the field, there were some adjustments!
Le premier jour, le brouillard, la nuit: The first day, fog, nightfall and a few snowflakes to try cramponing for 2 of my 3 companions. Epic adventure and impromptu initiation rite for them! Arrival at the small Fidelitas cabin well into the night, with well-hidden remains of wood (I had “optimized” the gas and could not afford an evening of melting snow) and the dry toilets full. It smells like the end of the season.
Le deuxième jour, le brouillard épais, e: The second day, the thick fog, again but without night this time. And an acute disorientation that pushes me inexorably to the left without even realising it, both up and down. When we finally pass below the layer, everyone seems to find their breathing, and their minds. The Martin-Busch-Hütte is already occupied by two Germans, who are very friendly, especially since they have already heated the hut!
Grand vallon enneigé encadré de sommets: Large snowy valley framed by peaks in the clouds, stage Fidelitas Hütte – Martin-Busch-Hütte, in the Ötztal Alps in Austria.
Petit changement de programme pour le tr: Small change of programme for the third day. In view of the form of the troops, we decide to reduce ambitions. And it will ultimately be a very good choice. We are at a ridge line from the Hochjoch-Hospiz, and we opt for the summit of Saykogel, which makes it easy to make the switch. The last part is a small ridge to cramp on, yet another novelty for my companions. And as a bonus, the best descent of the trip welcomes us on the other side. The dry, sun-drenched terrace is an invitation to a good coffee!

My favourite, more cavalier, is to cross the border via the island of Corfu, taking the ferry to Corfù this evening, then taking a second ferry to Sarenda early the next day. But we don't have the courage, and prefer to keep company with Iris, who takes her ferry back late in the evening.
L'autre solution consiste à prendre un b: The other option is to take a bus from Igoumenitsa to Saranda. There is just an option with a bus passing early in the morning to drop us off.
Ainsi, dès 4h30, nous nous tenons au poi: So, from 4:30 a.m., we stand at the point indicated by the bus company. La barrière est fermée. La frontière est: The barrier is closed. The border is closed at night and only opens at 8am. A closed border. As Europeans, members of the Schengen area and the European Union, this seems strange to us, such control to move from one country to another. But by moving from Greece to Albania, we are effectively leaving the EU. The controls are therefore stricter than here.
Il nous faut sortir du bus et montrer no: We have to get out of the bus and show our passports. Twice rather than once: first time on the Greek side, then a second time on the Albanian side.
Je vois le timing avancer. Je pensais po: I see the timing moving forward. However, I thought I had a considerable margin: departure at 4:30 a.m., more or less 1h30 drive. À présent, je regarde frénétiquement le: Now I'm frantically checking the GPS and I feel like our second connection is going to pass us by. So I go to see the driver to explain my problem to him. For him, there is no problem: he calls the company office to hold our next bus. But this one just left.
En arrivant à Saranda, nous patientons q: Arriving in Saranda, we wait a few minutes, then a solution is found. There is never a problem here. We got in a taxi and joined the bus we were supposed to take, which was waiting for us a few kilometres further. Well, the driver doesn't seem very happy with the situation.
Il nous faudra un peu plus de trois heur: It will take us a little over three hours to reach Tirana and meet up with the rest of the team. There, Pedro is waiting for us with his big Mercedes bus, and it is with him that we will finish this long crossing of Albania.

Lorsque nous passons à Lepushë, dans la: When we pass Lepushë, in the dark Albanian night, I try to perceive the snow limit. Ce soir, nous dormons à Vermosh. Mère et: Tonight we sleep in Vermosh. Mother and daughter welcome us to a guest house that, at home, we could describe as an agriturismo. Ce matin, c'est la jeune fille qui s'occ: This morning, it's the young girl who takes care of our breakfast. She is also the one who speaks French. Vermosh ne compte pas de centre-bourg. L: Vermosh does not have a town centre. The houses are scattered across a valley floor, now completely cleared of snow. This morning, we will have to walk a little before we can put on our skis. Fortunately, the presence of a forest track will allow us to wear shoes lower than the actual continuous snow limit.
Je craignais que les forêts soient trop: I was worried that the forests would be too dense to ski. This is partly the case, and some forests are skiable, but it is very difficult to assess their density just by observing aerial images.

Elle s'étire le long d'une crête dégarni: It stretches along a bare ridge, but where the forest tries to colonize on both sides. The snow, just flaked, is excellent.
Étonnement, Aurélien n'est plus dans mes: Surprisingly, Aurélien is no longer on my skis. Seconds pass, and soon Damien arrives. Paolo nous accueille. Un grand gaillard: Paolo welcomes us. A big guy who must be in his late thirties, with short-cut hair. He helped me organise this trip, especially managing the taxi. Bientôt, il semble que la musique sort d: Soon it seems like music is coming from everywhere. Speakers outside, emitting RNB sounds modified with a contemporary twist, a treat. Du sommet, la vue est fantastique. Nous: From the top, the view is fantastic. We are in the heart of this impressive massif that is the Prokletije. Before us stands an imposing limestone wall. La pente sud, raide et continue, semble: The southern slope, steep and continuous, looks delicious. Change of plan, we will take advantage of it and we will advise of a possible extension of the day at its base. From here, I don't see anything very obvious, but we'll see.
En bas de la pente, nous rejoignons un p: At the bottom of the slope, we reach a small plateau. The surrounding slopes crush us. One of the options imagined does not inspire me, a collector of wet snow avalanches, which will probably not wait until the next day to receive new snowfalls.
Reste le versant d'en face, où les ressa: There remains the slope opposite, where the steep jumps seem to be able to be crossed on skis.
En lisant la carte, j'ai l'impression qu: Reading the map, I have the impression that we could go up a few hundred metres and go back down due north, in order to optimize the snow limit. But after 200m of elevation gain, we arrive at a ridge, topped by an imposing monolith. On the other side, a steep slope of which we can't even see the bottom, and which gives us all, in turn, a few chills! Je tente une franche traversée, mais cel: I attempt a clear crossing, but it seems too exposed for the group. I turn back and try just below. Last chance by crossing on the right. The passage is a bit daring, but we have a rope and there is only 2 m of dry skiing. This will allow me to test the group, some of which I don't know. And in any case, I don't really want to go back up.
En bas du pierrier, la forêt de hêtres e: At the bottom of the scree, the beech forest is so dense that we are forced to take off our shoes. First contacts with the Albanian forest, which I had immediately identified as a critical and uncertain point when I designed the route.
Nous arrivons à ski au petit village de: We arrive on skis at the small village of Škala, where we meet Aurélien. Une femme et un homme, plus âgé qu'elle,: A woman and a man, older than her, come to welcome us. Neither of them speaks English, and we communicate with our hands. Dinner is ordered for 18:30, that's the main thing. We are starving. In the meantime, the fridge is full of beers…
L'équipe rit. Elle rit car après avoir f: The team laughs. Pour prendre notre dîner, nous pénétrons: To have our dinner, we enter another small chalet, below. We were thinking of visiting our hosts, but they live in Plav, the slightly larger town half an hour away.
La table se remplit de mets, dont un cer: The table is filled with dishes, including a certain number for which we are already accustomed, such as tomato and cucumber salad, and meat. Du col, un grand couloir, large et raide: From the pass, a large couloir, wide and steep, allows you to switch to Vusanje. I am vigilant for the slightest sound of pouring, and take great care to find regrouping points that are as protected as possible. Suddenly, I see with my own eyes what I don't like to see: a piece of cornice, fortunately not very big, breaks away from the crest. He won't come to us.
Je suis plutôt soulagé de rejoindre la z: I am rather relieved to reach the wooded area, even if it is dense and awkward. The trail shown on the map is not, but we are starting to get used to it. Several successive circular craters in the heart of the forest challenge us. First, we think of a natural phenomenon. The Prokletije massif is largely limestone and sinkholes are not rare. But their very regular shape and their arrangement, almost in series, quickly make us doubt.
Ces trous pourraient bien être les vesti: These holes could well be the remains of a much more recent episode in the history of the Balkans.
Au printemps 1999, pendant la guerre du: In the spring of 1999, during the Kosovo War, these Prokletije mountains saw thousands of Kosovar civilians fleeing the fighting. Entire families crossed these reliefs on foot to reach Albania. Many walked at night, guided by valley dwellers, crossing passes over 2,000 metres in the late winter snow. At the same time, the Yugoslav army attempted to control these passages, and some positions in these mountains were bombed.
La vallée qui accueille le village de Vu: The valley which accommodates the village of Vusanje is open and less austere than Škala. A little lower in altitude, spring has taken hold there for a long time. A beautiful trout river flows there. It also feels good to find this less austere, and sometimes heavy, atmosphere of the steep slopes of the Prokletije. The small chapel and the cemetery, a vast field with a few scattered graves, make me doubt the dominant religion here. Looking closely at the bell tower, a partially erased crescent is painted there. This is confirmed by our evening hosts. In the village, the inhabitants are predominantly Sunni.
Lorsque j'arrive devant la Guest House,: When I arrive in front of the Guest House, there is no sign of life. I then see an old lady stick her head out of the half-open door of a small shed, then, when she sees me, turn back, as if trying to hide. Odd. I knock on the door, and someone actually comes to open it. A tall guy in his forties, close-cropped hair, not very verbose, perhaps because of his poor English. His father is more talkative, and speaks English quite well for his generation. And beyond that, we find in him the same humanity as in our previous hosts.
Le repas est servi sur la table, disposé: The meal is served on the table, placed between the kitchen and the TV area. A rolling news channel broadcasts terrible images of the war in the Middle East. The materiality of the conflict appears to us in the face, with the help of these animated images of incredible violence.

Since the day before, there has been this pot of spread lying around on the work surface, and which the patriarch wanted us to taste in all its sauces last night. He filled a big bowl with it this morning, and we had a blast!
J'aime les matins avant l'aurore. Tout s: I love mornings before dawn. Everything happens at that moment, when the calm of the night provides acute clairvoyance. I go down to the living room, where our host is already busy preparing breakfast. He reads my thoughts and offers me a coffee. She's the one who prepares it for me, on a small blueberry placed on the coffee table, in front of the TV already on at this early hour. I write and I observe. Breakfast is prepared by successive blows, interspersed with long pauses, where sometimes we exchange a few words. He's the one who takes care of it, but she's never far away. These people are touching, in the positive sense of the word.
Nous repartons de Vusanje par une route: We leave Vusanje by a motorable road, but soon we have to reconnect with the Montenegrin forest. These beech forests are beautiful, but we like to get out of them... The terrain is still as complex, with micro reliefs not documented on the map. The weather forecast for the day kept changing. She announced a morning slot the day before, then a morning slot when she woke up this morning. It rained last night, and the sky has now darkened. A first rumble, in the distance, calls out to me, and when a loud detonation and a flash of lightning strike just above the slope that we are going up, I understand that a storm is breaking out. At the beginning of March, I didn't expect it! This will be the only warning shot. The sleet that has been falling for a good half hour now has deposited a few centimeters which should brighten up our descents, and fortunately, the sky is breaking and visibility is opening up again. Which is not a bad thing for dealing with this complex terrain.
À présent, nous remontons une vaste comb: Now, we go up a vast, not very steep valley, to the Čafa e Furumit pass. Anne-Laure and Aurel prefer to preserve their respective ailments, and we quickly climb to Maja e Rosit (2522m) until Arnaud and Damien join us at the pass. A delicious spring snow adorns this new descent, then comes the time when it is necessary to optimize the snow cover. The slope we are crossing is ravaged by avalanches of wet snow. It is always an uncertain pleasure to evolve in these balls, fortunately a little softened.
Il nous faudra une petite demi-heure de: It will take us about half an hour's walk to reach Kucaj, a small hamlet where two families live just above Valbonë, an essential place for ski touring in Albania. We are greeted by a young woman who speaks English well, like all the Albanians of this generation that we have met since the start of our journey. Tourism has become the only economic activity in these remote villages. But in Kucaj we are the first of winter, and probably the only ones. The potential of ski touring is enormous here, more so than in the other valleys visited.
Comme les deux nuits précédentes, nous m: Like the two previous nights, we eat in their living room, on the coffee table, served by a mother and her daughter. A feast, again. Especially this kind of broccoli pie. As usual, the huge flat screen, disproportionate to the size of the room, broadcasts clips. This time traditional music.
Ce matin, en ouvrant la porte d'entrée,: This morning, when I opened the front door, the fresh smell of tobacco assaulted my still sleeping senses. A man in his fifties, probably the father, is seated on the sofa. He puffs frantically on his industrial cigarette. The TV is still on, but this time it is showing other types of clips, where women's bodies are highlighted.
Il est né là, dans cette maison construi: He was born there, in this house built at the beginning of the 20th century. He draws “1911” in the palm of my hand. Then he shows us the new features: new rooms with double beds and thick mattresses, which contrast with our dormitory and its spring mattresses topped with soft foam, testifying to a real move upmarket in these tourist accommodations, probably correlated with a demand in this direction. Not ours anyway. He seems very happy to see us, a small variation of a daily life that is surely quite lonely in the winter in these remote mountains.
Nous repartons en basket. Trop fatigué p: We're going back to basketball. Too tired to continue at this pace, Arnaud prefers to take a break. Changing countries almost every day, on either side of this border ridge, it is not as simple as a star trip would be. I therefore offer him several options, and the chosen one consists of accompanying him to Vusanje, where he will spend the next two nights. He will join us in Babino Polje by taxi to finish the last stage together. Burning is a widespread practice here, and up to high altitudes, fields have been burned, leaving a persistent smell of sulfur. We go up a wide valley to Qafa Prosllopit, allowing us to switch again to the Vusanje valley left the day before. After accompanying Arnaud to the bottom of the snow, I join the other part of the group at the summit of Maja e Fazlis (2194m), where the uncertain path which must lead us to Cerem begins. As is often the case during this crossing, the forest turns out to be the problematic point, especially on the descent. A first area, barely colored on my map, is already steep and barely passes between the jumps. I fear for the next crux, tinged with a slightly darker yellow. Above all, I hesitate between two small parallel valleys. The map does not help me to take one option rather than another, but the aerial image rather convinces me of the option on the left, the one on the right seeming more rocky. After some acrobatics to cross an area of ​​dense vegetation, we find ourselves above an impassable jump. Failure. We turn back, and the other option turns out to be much more convenient. The rocks that appeared in the aerial image were in fact just a vast scree, nothing like the escarpment that I imagined at the time. Not without difficulty, we manage to overcome the uncertainties of the plant cover and join a snow-covered forest track up to the village of Cerem. I just scored a good point for Anne-Laure, who HATES putting skis AND boots on the backpack.
Nous sommes accueillis devant un grand b: We are greeted in front of a large building with chick-yellow shutters. A “diffuse” guest house where each small building has its function: kitchen on one side, living room in another, dining and sleeping area in the large building. The living room is a small wooden cabin with a slightly sloping floor, heated by a small, extremely efficient wood stove. Above the curtain rod, in the dark paneling of the room, sat a large, improbable portrait. A woman with voluminous hair and eighties-style makeup looked at us with a frozen smile. Draped in a shiny purple fabric, it looked like it had stepped out of an old glamor magazine. There was something deliciously incongruous about his presence. The meal is gargantuan: a dozen guests could sit there without anyone lacking anything, an indication among others of this generosity in the welcome. After dinner, we return to the small living room for our now traditional digestive belote tournament. Our hosts sit with us around the small coffee table, and we exchange looks and the fact of being together, much more than words, rare and translated into gestures and mimes. This warm presence is pleasant. Tomorrow will be the longest day. About thirty kilometres and not far from 2000m from ascent.
Rencontre avec un habitant à Valbonë lor: Meeting with a resident in Valbonë during a ski traverse of the Prokletije
J'aime ces journées où le relief se déve: I love these days when the relief develops for a long time under our feet. These days where we cross passes and ridges, where the terrain changes as we progress. These days when you have to be cunning to cover as much of the distance as possible on the descent. These days that start early and end late, and where the aperitif represents a form of accomplishment.
Une première montée nous mène au sommet: A first climb takes us to the top of B24, not without reminding Damien of one of the music groups that rocked his younger years, and Aurélien of the usefulness of the ski crampons that he did not take with him. A beautiful descent then drops us at the origin of a long wooded ridge, which we will ride for the next few hours between Montenegro and Albania. From the top of “B26”, the view opens onto the vast, gentle valley of Doberdoll, which was once an option for a stopover. I preferred Gacaferi, behind the border ridge, on the Kosovar side, because the hut looked great, and I wanted to mix the three border countries in this crossing of the Prokletije. These prokletijes, so steep in the first part of the journey, now completely changed in relief to offer more rounded summits and this vast, not very steep valley of Doberdoll. An ideal playground for snowmobiles, which reign supreme, offering us the pleasure of noise and smell, and the furious desire to escape! One of them comes to meet us at that moment, his knee resting on the seat of his snowmobile, as if to watch over visitors to the place who might not be as noisy as them. In humid heat we climb the steep southern slope above us, giving access to this new border, materialized as since the beginning of the day by a geographical watershed.
Gacaferi est un petit hameau de montagne: Gacaferi is a small mountain hamlet, where the Kosovar flag flutters in the wind. For the first time since the start of this crossing, we are not the only skiers: two other groups of young English people are soon joined by the couple we met by chance in Vusanje two days earlier. She is Chinese and lived in Pau for nine years before moving to Trentino-Alto Adige to join him, a young Italian mountain guide who speaks almost not a word of the language of Dante and Petrarch.
Nous sommes frappés de la qualité de l'a: We are struck by the quality of the welcome. So certainly, there is not the charm of the “homestay” welcome that we experienced the previous evenings in all the villages we passed through, but here, nothing is left to chance in the attention paid to the comfort of the visitor. The bar is self-service, with everyone recording their drinks in a small notebook. A lounge area has several comfortable sofas, arranged in circles and facing a large opening onto the mountains, and the dinner, prepared in particular by the mother of Adriatik, the caretaker, is unequivocally the best since the start of our crossing. The buffet is a great test of self-control, and very often ends with the same observation: “well, we're going to sleep on our backs tonight..!” ". There is such diversity and it is so well cooked that it is not easy not to try every dish. Even our dog has never been so fed, and that's probably what will lead him to abandon us.
Le refuge de Gacaferi n'a que des qualit: The Gacaferi hut only has good qualities, except that of forcing us to have breakfast from 8am. Too late for spring conditions, and too late for today's weather forecast, conditions for which are expected to deteriorate from midday. Despite everything, I am not changing the ambitions of the day, planning the ascents of Maja e Ropes (2502m) and Maja e Qenit (2405m). As we plunge the beautiful ridge of the first summit, grey cumulus clouds form at an impressive speed. We switch to the eastern slope for a beautiful descent which takes us away from our cape, but a forest track allows us to go around the mountain at a lower cost to reach a small alpine hamlet where many constructions are recent, testifying to a marked interest in these mountain spaces. At the entrance to the village, an old Renault R5 has been modified to equip it with caterpillars. The weather seems to be hesitant, between clouds and clearings, sleet and dry weather. From the summit the long valley of Babino Polje unfolds under our skis. A hamlet that Michel Parmentier evokes in his story. The descent is delicious, transformed into snow. On the other hand, a continuous belt of fir trees blocks access to the bottom of the valley. These are not spruce trees with high branches, but perfect cones whose lower branches touch the ground, and very often those of their neighbours. It is a precision ski that must be deployed and cunning to find the way through this labyrinth. Fortunately, the belt is not wide, and we reach the bottom of the valley and its track, groomed in its centre by the successive passages of Lada, whose lower body touches as the ruts of the wheels deepen.
Nous retrouvons Arnaud, venu à notre ren: We find Arnaud, who came to meet us on this track. The hamlet of Babino Polje has 4 or 5 houses, on the other side of the river, and around fifteen others are built along the track, including our guest house. A complex that appears massive to us, made up of several small two-storey houses attached to each other, and a building of 4 or 5 floors, immense, disproportionate compared to the other buildings in the valley. It reminds me of Asian buildings, with its three successive hipped roofs, intersecting the top three floors. Its construction is not completed, it even seems far from being finished. Surprisingly, part of the roof is missing on its front part, further reinforcing this feeling of incompleteness. We are greeted by a young couple. She is fully pregnant with their fourth child.
Contrairement aux autres hébergements, o: Unlike other accommodations, where it is often elderly or very young people who take care of us, here the pace seems much more sustained. They don't seem bored. Three children, and soon four, a huge construction site that the husband is leading alone, and a guest house to manage all year round: all this leaves little respite. Besides, we feel they are a little overwhelmed. Everything here seems to be done in haste, and that raises questions for me.
Dans notre petit dortoir, la douche a ét: In our small dormitory, the shower was dismantled. The husband tries to bring it back up for us, but in the end, there will only be hot water — too hot. So we will go and shower in the shared shower. And here again, you shouldn't be too fussy about the construction details: the tiling is not very well laid, the shower, with rain option, does not work, there is no moisture evacuation system...
Dans la pièce qui sert de réfectoire, un: In the room that serves as a refectory, an umbrella-type gas heater attempts to warm the space, without much success. Here again, the ground is sloping — and what a slope.
Tous ces petits éléments nous donnent le: All these little elements give us the feeling of a life led at a frantic pace. Perhaps by connecting certain details, a form of coherence appears: the big Q7, old generation, parked in the courtyard, the Moncler polo shirt, the latest generation Samsung Ultra, and then this disproportionate construction.
Tout cela semble converger vers un même: All this seems to converge towards the same horizon: a quest for greatness, undoubtedly abundance or wealth. But sometimes, perhaps, it is better to keep another measure, otherwise we risk falling into approximate excess.
Quand bien même, nous sommes bien reçus,: Even so, we are well received, very well indeed. After showering we are invited to have tea or coffee in the small space which also serves as a kitchen and bedroom for the whole family. This is the ground floor of one of the small houses.
La porte d'entrée frotte sur le linoléum: The front door rubs against the linoleum. You have to lift it slightly to open it. There, we enter a room which, on one side, is equipped for cooking, and on the other where sofas will be transformed, in the evening, into a large bed for the whole family.
Au fond, une petite véranda vitrée accue: At the back, a small glass veranda accommodates a table and two benches. It is in this small space that we will spend the afternoon playing cards, pleasantly warmed by the wood stove and by a small circular oven placed on the floor, in which our host bakes his rolls.
Je laisse le groupe pour aller effectuer: I leave the group to go do a little scouting. Tomorrow, we will not have time to test: we will have to go for the most efficient one, because the day is timed. A few hours of skiing in the morning, then, around 1 or 14:00 at the latest, the taxi must come and pick us up to take us back to Durrës, from where we board the ferry that same evening.
Plusieurs options sont possibles. J'ai c: Several options are possible. I chose the simplest, the least uncertain - perhaps not the most beautiful or obvious line - but the one which I am sure will not deliver any surprises. Especially since the weather forecast for the next day is uncertain, and it will probably be the least beautiful day since the start of the crossing.
Lorsqu'il est 6h du matin, nous pénétron: When it is 6 a.m., we enter the family's living space again. The sofas have been deployed and everyone is sleeping on this large sleeping surface. Everyone, except the mother, who kindly agreed to serve us breakfast immediately. She even prepared pancakes for us that were still steaming, placed on the plate in the middle of the table.
Avant de partir, on nous remet ce qui s': Before leaving, we are given what will prove to be a precious sesame: the paper which authorizes us to enter Montenegro from Albania without going through one of the official border posts. At my request, the husband went to pick him up for us last night in Plav.
Pour monter au sommet du Starac, j'avais: To climb to the top of Starac, I therefore had two options. One was to go east and go through an area of ​​dense forest that looked very steep to me on the map. The other, going around to the west, was to go up gentle slopes to Javorsko Brdo, then follow a broad shoulder to the summit. It’s this simpler option that I liked.
Du sommet, nous basculons en versant nor: From the summit, we switch to the north slope to ski a delicious little layer of powder on a hard base. Then we cross straight towards the west, trying to avoid heavily wooded areas as much as possible. In this game, snowmobile tracks prove to be valuable clues, allowing me to connect the open spaces also spotted on my satellite images.
Nous remettons une dernière fois les pea: We put the skins on one last time to climb to the top of Djevojački krš. From here, we have a magnificent view of the entire wide valley which borders the Prokletije. In the middle of it, there is the magnificent Plav Lake. And at the very bottom, our starting point eight days ago, a little hidden by the numerous clouds which are gradually piling up on the summits.
Nous commençons à descendre une large ar: We begin to descend a wide ridge of spring snow and, quickly, I realise that this is not the one I wanted to follow. The other is hidden by the fog which gradually invades all the peaks. So we turn off and enter another fir forest. But in this one, the trees are relatively spaced out and skiing is rather easy.
Damien has just had a great flight. He had not seen a small break in the slope caused by the effect of the wind. He dislocated his shoulder. He recovers instantly. Damien looks really bad: he hardly expresses anything, but I feel that he is in pain.
Je ralentis le rythme pour finir ce pass: I slow down the pace to finish this not so easy section to ski. At the bottom of the forest, we join a track, then, from the track, the road to the Čakor pass, starting point for Michel and Périllat during their big ski traverses of the 80s. Original inspiration for this travel project. I think about it and it doesn't leave me indifferent.
À présent, nous descendons sur les bas-c: Now we go down to the sides of this road, partly cleared of snow. Soon, after a turn, it seems to me that a car is parked in the middle of the road. Strange for a road that seems passable. And as I get closer, I understand.
Dessus, il est écrit « policija ». Sur l: On it it says “policija”. On the two front seats, two police officers seem to be waiting for us. When they see us, the passenger in the car gets out, and I know very well what he is going to ask me. Even before he does, I take out my passport and ask my companions to do the same.
Et puis je lui tends aussi ce précieux s: And then I also hand him this precious sesame, which I am happy to have had the foresight to ask for - helped a little by the discussion I had with our host from Skala on the third evening. Without him, I might not have thought about it, because last year we went from Albania to Macedonia, then from Macedonia to Kosovo, without going through the official border posts, and yet we left via Pristina even though we had arrived via Tirana.
Les deux policiers emportent nos passepo: The two police officers took our passports into the car and, after a few minutes, they returned them to us. A priori, we pass this check without incident.
Je leur demande confirmation — non sans: I ask them for confirmation – not without difficulty and thanks to Google Translate – that the taxi will be able to pick us up at the end of the plowed road. I don't quite understand the response, but it seems to me that it is rather positive, whereas they were quite austere when they approached us.
Ils se sont bien détendus en voyant que: They relaxed when they saw that we were in order and even smiled when I made a mistake in the Google Translate buttons and made them repeat their answer.
Alors que nous attendons le taxi, un gro: As we wait for the taxi, a large pick-up pulling a trailer on which a buggy is placed stops alongside us. Inside, two men in military fatigues, rather smiling. They present themselves as border guards. They are already aware of our presence here and ask us if this is where we are waiting for the taxi.
Il est midi et demi pile lorsque nous ar: It is precisely half past twelve when we arrive, exactly the time I had sent this morning to our taxi driver.
Le chauffeur de taxi ne parle pas un mot: The taxi driver doesn't speak a word of English. He only asks me: “Where are you from?” » I explain to him that we have to stop on the way, at Lepushë, to collect all our luggage. I try to write this to him on Google Translate, but, unsure whether he has understood my request correctly, he calls a friend — a local guide from ski touring living in Plav, who speaks perfect English.
J'explique donc à notre interprète impro: So I explain to our improvised interpreter that we simply have to stop at Lepushë to collect our things.
Notre chauffeur a une fâcheuse tendance: Our driver has an annoying tendency to look at his phone and, at one point, it couldn't be missed. He doesn't see the car stopped in front of us. Fortunately I make a movement with my hand to grab the steering wheel and jerk to the right so that he finally reacts. It was time.
En arrivant au port, il semble complètem: When he arrives at the port, he seems completely lost. I send him a Google Maps link and, apparently, this is the first time he has used this application. Moreover, when he finally manages to drop us off more or less at the desired location, he asks me to send him a link to leave the port and return home. He obviously didn't know how to use Google Maps. For a taxi driver, this is still a shame.
Le taxi va nous mener au ferry à Durrës,: The taxi will take us to the ferry in Durrës, where we will have just time to buy something to eat before boarding. The ferry will disembark us in Bari, in the south of Italy, and we will barely have time, after going through customs, to take a bus to the central station. Here again, we will just have time to buy something to eat before boarding the train which will take us to Milan.
À Milan, nous aurons tout juste le temps: In Milan, we will just have time to change platforms to take a last train from the Trenord company which will take us to Novara. This is where there might be the one little grain of sand. Indeed, when leaving for the ferry, I wanted to move my car so as not to leave it in the same place for two weeks. It made a weird noise, then it stalled. She told me: "It's probably the battery", but I still had my doubts, since the car had started before stopping.

Itinérance #11 — Traversée du Dammastock: Journeying #11 — Crossing the Dammastock, or when the planets align
La saison n'est pas tout à fait terminée: The season isn't quite over, but it will probably be the journey that will have had the biggest impact on me. We were initially supposed to go to the Bernina massif, but due to lack of snow, we had to fall back on a plan B, and what a plan B!
Sur la route de l'Ubaye, trois jours ava: On the road to Ubaye, three days before leaving, I was actively thinking about the replacement project, tracing routes towards the Nufenenpass, the Tödi, the Dammastock or the Susa valley. A little to the north, a little to the south, since the weather continued to play with our nerves (especially mine, for a good month, because the customers, a priori, trust me!).
Notre principal avantage : partir 5 jour: Our main advantage: going 5 days a week, which means you have no trouble booking. Well, that's what I thought!
Las de ne pas trouver la ligne idéale, e: Tired of not finding the ideal line, and a little pressed for time, I fell back on the classic crossing of the Dammastock, a little ashamed all the same to follow an already existing guidebook. Seeing space in all the shelters, I was quick to reserve them.
Le lendemain, donc la veille du départ,: The next day, the day before departure, translating the confirmation emails for security reasons, I was disappointed to see that my reservation request for the first hut received a negative response. Albert-Heim was full… Panic on board! I had to dive back into the maps.
Plan A : Sidelenhütte. Pas de local d'hi: Plan A: Sidelenhütte. No winter room, closed.
Plan B : hôtel Tiefenbach. Premier jour: Plan B: Hotel Tiefenbach. First day cooler but 1800 m the next day… meh.
Plan C : Salbithütte, mais J2 long, tech: Plan C: Salbithütte, but D2 long, technical and adventurous. In short, I like it but I must not be the only one to be jubilant! The team must follow me in this idea, and I present both plans to them in complete transparency. Unanimous opinion: we want adventure, go! And what's more, it greatly facilitates the logistics of return transport.
J1 : montée à la Salbithütte. 500 m de m: D1: climb to Salbithütte. 500 m walk then the rest in the fog. Not memorable, but like any first day of raiding. On the other hand, we discover a heated cabin and cupboards full of beers!
J2 : une journée mémorable ! Entre solei: D2: a memorable day! Between sunshine and drifting cloud, I am in my element behind the lens. Two couloirs climbed with skis on the pack, then two more, a good 40° steep, to ski in fine spring snow. And between them, a magnificent glacier to climb and 700 m of untouched north-facing powder!

Ce raid-là, plus encore que d'autres déj: This raid, even more than others already complicated to organise this year, was a headache. Over the 4 projected days, the weather forecast announced an active return from the East to the Italian border and a disturbance from the West affecting the central and western Alps. Only Austria was spared. We had in any case planned to visit the Tyrolean Ortles, and in comparison the western part of Austria is more accessible.
Sauf que je n'ai jamais mis les pieds en: Except that I have never set foot in Austria, and keeping the ethics that I apply to the other massifs that I visit, I refrain from going to the sites of commercial agencies to copy and paste an already ready-made raid. On the contrary, I want to virtually immerse myself in a massif, understand its relief and the "areas of weakness", identify possible accommodation... In any case, I wanted to favour a secondary massif this time, out of an imperative need to escape the crowds of the Easter weekend.
En balayant grossièrement les différents: Roughly scanning the different Austrian massifs, looking for those which did not have too alpine a profile, I stopped on Vorarlberg.
Ensuite, il a fallu gérer le casse-tête: Then, we had to manage the accommodation headache. Between accommodations whose winter premises are closed until further notice, those where you need to collect a key and those which do not have a winter premises, the choice is not great. There were exactly three left, far enough from each other to imagine beautiful stages. Only problem, the first of them will be long... second problem: if we flee the bad weather, we will not be spared by the wind...

Le troisième jour restera dans la mémoir: The third day will remain in the memory of my companions as the most beautiful day. We played ridge jump, going up south and down into the nice cold snow that fell during the night. First the Valschavieljöchle, as a warm-up, then the beautiful northern slope of the Schwarze Wand and finally another beautiful slope of an unnamed bump.
Arrivés à la Reutlinger Hütte, la seule: Arriving at the Reutlinger Hütte, the only cabin where I was able to reserve places, we found the first closed door. We clear a second door, hoping that it will be open. But after half an hour of work, we have to come to the same conclusion... The cabin is closed, and at no time was this indicated on the internet. The caretaker only sent me an email to warn me that the supply of wood was almost exhausted, but she never mentioned the presence of a possible key. Worry overwhelms me. Ideas flow quickly in the boys' heads, but with much more foresight in that of Cécile, who puts forward the idea of ​​trying the key used for the first cabin. We won't need to use any other stratagems. The door opens, and we all breathe a big sigh of relief!
Cette petite cabane est bien plus rustiq: This little cabin is much more rustic than the previous one, but it embodies the imagination of the cabin: a large table and on the other side a large dormitory which occupies the entire width. This is the first time in 3 days that no one has heated the cabin for us, and we feel the 1°C displayed on the interior thermometer. We will climb painfully to 8°C, and not a tenth more! It serves even more as a shelter because the storm is raging outside. Its location, in the middle of a pass, is perhaps not for nothing in the vibration of the walls with each gust. The wind manages to rush into the micro-interstices of the walls and the floor and even to open the double entrance door, although it is closed.

It’s going to be an atmosphere! And yet, a few hundred metres below the pass, there is no longer a breath. On the other hand, rain soon replaces the snow, and we are now progressing in a flimsy coat.
Une à une, les options anticipées sont r: One by one, the anticipated options are rendered obsolete. One slope does not inspire me, another was swept away by a deep avalanche, yet another is plunged into fog. The option ultimately chosen had never been identified. As far as possible, I try to reach and then cross the ridge which separates me from Langen, because the descent seems much less difficult.
C'est finalement dans une pente labyrint: It is ultimately through a labyrinthine slope that we achieve our goals. How I love these descents punctuated with uncertainty!

Restait à trouver un cheminement réalisa: All that remained was to find a feasible way through these mountains, rarely, if ever, visited on skis.

Je suis venu en Géorgie pour la première: I first came to Georgia in 2014 to explore the possibilities for para-alpinism. We climbed wherever we felt drawn, setting off for several days to try a summit we had spotted from afar, attracted by its slender outline.
Après quatre jours au pied de ces montag: After four days beneath those immense mountains, we returned without that summit, but with other fine rocky ridges and a storm in the tent that we still remember… Checking our information afterwards, we realised we had been two valleys out!

En 2019, j’étais revenu avec ma compagne: In 2019, I returned with my partner to test clothing for Pyrenex. We had a free hand; we just had to go somewhere cold. Relatively cold, as it turned out: by late May and early June, summer had already reached the Caucasus.

D’abord, à l’est, les hauts plateaux vol: First, in the east, the high volcanic plateaux of Javakheti. Open, fairly gentle terrain, set very high, between Bakuriani, Tabatskouri, Samsari and Abuli. Puis une traversée du pays par la route: Then a drive across the country to the west, where the setting changes completely. In Adjara and Guria, the mountains are more wooded, the valleys deeper and the snow far more abundant. Bakhmaro is now known to skiers and for cat-skiing, but what interests me lies elsewhere: at the edges, in the gaps, in valleys where it is still possible to link villages on skis, from Utkhisubani to Danisparauli, then Ghorjomi and Bakhmaro.

Avec Antoine, on s’était dit qu’on ferai: Antoine and I once said we would travel through the ‘-stan’ countries together. That was a long time ago, when my commitments in life were rather different. Since then, I have married and had children. Life, really!
En 2025, presque sur un coup de tête, j’: In 2025, almost on a whim, I put together a trip to Kazakhstan after discovering a network of unstaffed huts in the Ile Alatau mountains, just south of Almaty, the country’s economic capital.
Nous avions commencé le voyage dans une: We began in a ski resort that looked in every respect like one of our Alpine resorts. The change of scene we had come for would have to wait. But not for long.
Après avoir passé le premier bivouac et: After the first bivouac shelter and the last snowmobile tracks, we crossed into another world. A glacial world, immense and wild.
À quelques encablures de la frontière ki: Not far from the Kyrgyz border, I was caught out. A patch of ice beneath a deceptive layer of snow, and then a fall, endless and uncontrolled. I hit the rock. The only rock on the slope. My thigh took the impact, with all the momentum of the fall.
Instants de doute, là où rien ne doit ar: Moments of doubt, in a place where nothing must go wrong. My femur? I can stand, but how it hurts. We are in the middle of nowhere, with nobody to rely on.
Et comme tous les après-midi, le brouill: And, as every afternoon, fog soon closes around us and snow begins to fall…
Le Kazakhstan a été une expérience initi: Kazakhstan was an initiation. I wanted to return to those Central Asian countries. So I began looking for mountains suited to ski touring and multi-day journeys.
J’ai préparé un voyage au Kirghizistan,: I prepared a trip to Kyrgyzstan, but winter-accessible yurts at $150 a night — per person — felt too much like tourist traps.
Et puis je suis tombé sur le récit d’un: Then I came across an account by a guide friend, Fabien Artero, one of the first to go there. He had spent several days in the little village of Kul’, east of Samarkand and north of the Hissar mountains.
Une exploration systématique des village: A systematic search through the villages of these mountains soon made one thing clear: tourism is barely developed here, and finding accommodation would not be easy.
Pour la première fois, il m’a fallu soll: For the first time, I had to turn to a local travel agency, through Sherali, an Uzbek who speaks fluent French.
Et mon envie de traverser intégralement: My wish to traverse the entire range from south to north ran into two major constraints: staying in ‘unofficial’ accommodation is very complicated, and walking anywhere near the Tajik border is strictly forbidden…
De ces contraintes est née une belle lig: From those constraints, a fine route emerged, through mountains that may never have seen skiers…

Du 31 janvier au 4 février 2022, le grou: From 31 January to 4 February 2022, the group travelled through Queyras from Arvieux to Abriès, via Aiguilles. Each day combined journeying with skiing and meetings with local residents and stakeholders: farmers, ski instructors, hoteliers, elected and former elected officials, technicians from the Regional Natural Park or tourism managers.

In Queyras, these two worlds were built together for a long time, before tourism became the dominant activity. The raid sought to understand the tensions, complementarities and new trajectories that are appearing today in the face of climate change.
Le parcours documenté : départ d’Arvieux: The documented route: departure from Arvieux, journeying towards Souliers then Aiguilles, before continuing towards Abriès. The project sources precisely document this crossing from Arvieux to Abriès via Aiguilles, with a stage and a meeting in Souliers; the detailed ski route pass by pass not being published, I prefer not to invent the intermediate passages.

Il faut être à l'aise en ski hors-piste: You must be comfortable skiing off-piste in varied snow conditions and have experience with the ski touring. The endurance and technical requirements then vary greatly from one trip to another.

Sur une itinérance, le rôle du guide con: On a multi-day journey, the guide's role is to prepare and then adapt a line over several days depending on the terrain, the snow and weather conditions and the group. On distant trips, this preparation also includes a significant part of local logistics.

La distance n'est plus seulement mesurée: Distance is no longer only measured in kilometres or in elevation : it is measured in days, in stages, in lights, in shared meals, in snow changes and in encounters.

comprendre le territoire, chercher les p: understand the territory, look for passages, identify accommodation, imagine variants, anticipate conditions and build a project adapted to the group.
